[{'type': 'input_text', 'text': 'Script completed\nWall time 20.7 seconds\nOutput:\n'}, {'type': 'input_text', 'text': '{"chunk_id":"ee48b6","wall_time_seconds":1.4942372,"exit_code":0,"original_token_count":8104,"output":"### lsat-u-topic-builder\\r\\n---\\r\\nname: lsat-u-topic-builder\\r\\ndescription: Audit-driven bootstrap for a new LSAT U topic bootcamp. Walks the topic\'s source corpus, tier-grades every file (S/A/B/C/D), scans the Mac for related files outside /Curriculum/, identifies content gaps, anchors the quality bar to Causation Station / Abstraction (coaching tone, comprehensive, guiding), then generates the project folder with audit findings baked into all four files. Use when Joshua wants to start a new LSAT U topic bootcamp (Causation, Comparison, Necessary Assumption, Conditional Logic, etc.) and have the build start from real corpus knowledge, not generic templates. Trigger phrases include \\"create a new LSAT U topic bootcamp\\", \\"spin up a [topic] bootcamp\\", \\"audit and init [topic]\\", \\"replicate Main Conclusion for [topic]\\", \\"scaffold [topic] project\\".\\r\\n---\\r\\n\\r\\n# LSAT U Topic Builder (v2: Audit-Driven Bootstrap)\\r\\n\\r\\n## When to use this skill\\r\\n\\r\\nTrigger when Joshua wants to start a new LSAT U topic bootcamp build. The skill replicates the Main Conclusion four-stage workflow into a new topic project, but does the work upfront so Claude Code starts Gate 0 with audited corpus, identified gaps, and topic-specific quality bar already established.\\r\\n\\r\\nDo NOT trigger mid-build on an existing topic, for shipped topic refactors, or for general workflow discussion.\\r\\n\\r\\n## What changed from v1\\r\\n\\r\\nv1 was folder bootstrap with placeholder templates. v2 actually does Stage 1 work (audit + grading + gap analysis) before generating files. Claude Code starts at Gate 0 with substantive context, not \\"TBD at Gate 1\\" everywhere.\\r\\n\\r\\nTrade-off: v2 takes ~20-40 minutes to run vs v1\'s ~3 minutes. The output is substantially better.\\r\\n\\r\\n## Three phases\\r\\n\\r\\n- **Phase A**: Topic Audit (scan, grade, gap-flag, Mac-wide search)\\r\\n- **Phase B**: Quality Benchmarking (anchor to Causation Station / Abstraction + external references; lock coaching tone)\\r\\n- **Phase C**: Project Bootstrap + Claude Code Handoff\\r\\n\\r\\n---\\r\\n\\r\\n## PHASE A: TOPIC AUDIT\\r\\n\\r\\n### A1. Inventory the topic folder\\r\\n\\r\\nBash-list `C:/Users/Joshu/dev/ai-os/raw/sources/lsat-curriculum/{Topic}/`. Capture:\\r\\n- Files in `Notes/`: filename, extension, file size, modification date\\r\\n- Files in `Homework/`: same\\r\\n- Any `_scan_*` files (later additions)\\r\\n- Any `_megadoc_*` files (pre-consolidated syntheses)\\r\\n- Any `_export_*/` folder (prior Cowork audit work — if exists, mine it as starting point)\\r\\n\\r\\nReport: total file count, breakdown by source type (original / megadoc / scan), list every file by name.\\r\\n\\r\\n### A2. Scan the rest of the Mac for related files NOT already in /Curriculum/{Topic}/\\r\\n\\r\\nTopics other than Main Conclusion may have related material scattered in other folders (Desktop, Downloads, iCloud Drive, other project folders). Find them.\\r\\n\\r\\n**Recommended approach (in order of preference):**\\r\\n\\r\\n1. **Spotlight via osascript** (driven by computer-use tool):\\r\\n   - Open Terminal, run `mdfind -name {topic-keyword} | grep -v \\"Curriculum/{Topic}/\\"`\\r\\n   - Examples for Causation: `mdfind \\"causation\\" -onlyin ~/Documents -onlyin ~/Desktop -onlyin ~/Downloads`\\r\\n   - Capture results, dedupe by filename + size match against /Curriculum/{Topic}/\\r\\n2. **Computer-use Finder Spotlight**:\\r\\n   - Open Finder, Cmd+Space for Spotlight, search topic keywords\\r\\n   - Filter results to file types: PDF, docx, md, txt\\r\\n   - Compare against existing corpus\\r\\n3. **Manual prompt to Joshua**:\\r\\n   - If automated scan isn\'t feasible, ask Joshua: \\"Are there topic-related files outside /Curriculum/{Topic}/ that should be scanned? Common spots: Desktop, Downloads, iCloud, other project folders.\\"\\r\\n\\r\\n**Filter for non-duplicates:**\\r\\n- Filename match against existing corpus\\r\\n- File-size match within 5% (catches near-duplicates with renames)\\r\\n- For PDFs, also compare first-100-bytes hash if size matches\\r\\n\\r\\n**Report:**\\r\\n- Found-and-relevant files (full path, why it looks relevant)\\r\\n- Found-but-likely-duplicate files (with the duplicate-of pointer)\\r\\n### example-command\\r\\n---\\r\\nname: example-command\\r\\ndescription: An example user-invoked skill that demonstrates frontmatter options and the skills/<name>/SKILL.md layout\\r\\nargument-hint: <required-arg> [optional-arg]\\r\\nallowed-tools: [Read, Glob, Grep, Bash]\\r\\n---\\r\\n\\r\\n# Example Command (Skill Format)\\r\\n\\r\\nThis demonstrates the `skills/<name>/SKILL.md` layout for user-invoked slash commands. It is functionally identical to the legacy `commands/example-command.md` format — both are loaded the same way; only the file layout differs.\\r\\n\\r\\n## Arguments\\r\\n\\r\\nThe user invoked this with: $ARGUMENTS\\r\\n\\r\\n## Instructions\\r\\n\\r\\nWhen this skill is invoked:\\r\\n\\r\\n1. Parse the arguments provided by the user\\r\\n2. Perform the requested action using allowed tools\\r\\n3. Report results back to the user\\r\\n\\r\\n## Frontmatter Options Reference\\r\\n\\r\\nSkills in this layout support these frontmatter fields:\\r\\n\\r\\n- **name**: Skill identifier (matches directory name)\\r\\n- **description**: Short description shown in /help\\r\\n- **argument-hint**: Hints for command arguments shown to user\\r\\n- **allowed-tools**: Pre-approved tools for this skill (reduces permission prompts)\\r\\n- **model**: Override the model (e.g., \\"haiku\\", \\"sonnet\\", \\"opus\\")\\r\\n\\r\\n## Example Usage\\r\\n\\r\\n```\\r\\n/example-command my-argument\\r\\n/example-command arg1 arg2\\r\\n```\\r\\n### example-skill\\r\\n---\\r\\nname: example-skill\\r\\ndescription: This skill should be used when the user asks to \\"demonstrate skills\\", \\"show skill format\\", \\"create a skill template\\", or discusses skill development patterns. Provides a reference template for creating Claude Code plugin skills.\\r\\nversion: 1.0.0\\r\\n---\\r\\n\\r\\n# Example Skill\\r\\n\\r\\nThis skill demonstrates the structure and format for Claude Code plugin skills.\\r\\n\\r\\n## Overview\\r\\n\\r\\nSkills are model-invoked capabilities that Claude autonomously uses based on task context. Unlike commands (user-invoked) or agents (spawned by Claude), skills provide contextual guidance that Claude incorporates into its responses.\\r\\n\\r\\n## When This Skill Applies\\r\\n\\r\\nThis skill activates when the user\'s request involves:\\r\\n- Creating or understanding plugin skills\\r\\n- Skill template or reference needs\\r\\n- Skill development patterns\\r\\n\\r\\n## Skill Structure\\r\\n\\r\\n### Required Files\\r\\n\\r\\n```\\r\\nskills/\\r\\n└── skill-name/\\r\\n    └── SKILL.md          # Main skill definition (required)\\r\\n```\\r\\n\\r\\n### Optional Supporting Files\\r\\n\\r\\n```\\r\\nskills/\\r\\n└── skill-name/\\r\\n    ├── SKILL.md          # Main skill definition\\r\\n    ├── README.md         # Additional documentation\\r\\n    ├── references/       # Reference materials\\r\\n    │   └── patterns.md\\r\\n    ├── examples/         # Example files\\r\\n    │   └── sample.md\\r\\n    └── scripts/          # Helper scripts\\r\\n        └── helper.sh\\r\\n```\\r\\n\\r\\n## Frontmatter Options\\r\\n\\r\\nSkills support these frontmatter fields:\\r\\n\\r\\n- **name** (required): Skill identifier\\r\\n- **description** (required): Trigger conditions - describe when Claude should use this skill\\r\\n- **version** (optional): Semantic version number\\r\\n- **license** (optional): License information or reference\\r\\n\\r\\n## Writing Effective Descriptions\\r\\n\\r\\nThe description field is crucial - it tells Claude when to invoke the skill.\\r\\n\\r\\n**Good description patterns:**\\r\\n```yaml\\r\\ndescription: This skill should be used when the user asks to \\"specific phrase\\", \\"another phrase\\", mentions \\"keyword\\", or discusses topic-area.\\r\\n```\\r\\n\\r\\n**Include:**\\r\\n### assign-lsatu-work\\r\\n---\\r\\nname: assign-lsatu-work\\r\\ndescription: Operate LSAT U headlessly. On Windows a newline drops `--dry-run` and sends for real\\r\\n  (this happened on 2026-09-23). The wrapper refuses it; do not work around it.\\r\\n\\r\\nGuided-drill catalog and MCP details live in the [guided workflow reference](references/guided-drill-workflow.md), including the authored-content exception and immediate fallback when new MCP tools have not appeared in a chat yet.\\r\\n### bootcamp-parity-audit\\r\\n---\\r\\nname: bootcamp-parity-audit\\r\\ndescription: Audit a given LSAT U bootcamp\'s feature and visual parity against the flagship Intro to LR (Main Conclusion) bootcamp, anchored to the quality bar doc. Use when Joshua asks to \\"compare against Intro to LR\\", \\"check parity\\", \\"audit [bootcamp name]\\", or wants to know how far a bootcamp is from shipped quality. Trigger with /bootcamp-parity-audit <bootcamp-name>.\\r\\n---\\r\\n\\r\\nAudit a named LSAT U bootcamp against the flagship Intro to LR (Main Conclusion) bootcamp and the shared quality bar, and report the delta.\\r\\n\\r\\n## Inputs\\r\\n\\r\\nThe bootcamp name/slug (e.g. \\"Abstract\\", \\"Flaw & Famous Flaws\\", \\"Causation Station\\"). If not given, ask which one, once, don\'t guess.\\r\\n\\r\\n## Anchor documents (read these first, in order)\\r\\n\\r\\n1. `~/ai-os/archive/wiki-pre-rebuild-2026-07-16/domains/lsat-u/synthesis/bootcamp-quality-bar.md` — the shared bar every bootcamp finishes to.\\r\\n2. `~/ai-os/archive/wiki-pre-rebuild-2026-07-16/domains/lsat-u/synthesis/intro-to-lr-product.md` — the flagship\'s product spec (what \\"done\\" looks like).\\r\\n3. `~/ai-os/archive/wiki-pre-rebuild-2026-07-16/domains/lsat-u/synthesis/intro-to-lr-design.md` — the flagship\'s design system (colors, type, role tokens).\\r\\n4. `~/ai-os/wiki/entities/intro-to-lr-bootcamp.md` if it exists, for entity-level facts.\\r\\n5. Whatever entity page exists for the target bootcamp under `wiki/entities/` — read it if present; if it doesn\'t exist yet, say so, that itself is a gap.\\r\\n\\r\\n## Codebase pass\\r\\n\\r\\nIn the LSATU repo (`C:/Users/Joshu/dev/ai-os-projects/lsatu/`):\\r\\n1. Find the target bootcamp\'s source directory under `src/bootcamps/`.\\r\\n2. Compare its file/component structure against the Intro to LR structure (`src/bootcamps/main-conclusion/`) at a glance, don\'t read every file, sample the key surfaces (overview, drill/practice flow, data layer).\\r\\n3. Note any surface Intro to LR has that the target bootcamp lacks entirely.\\r\\n\\r\\n## Output: 5-point delta report\\r\\n\\r\\nJoshua\'s preferred format (per past sessions):\\r\\n\\r\\n```\\r\\n1. Feature parity: <what Intro to LR has that this bootcamp is missing>\\r\\n2. Visual parity: <design-system deviations from intro-to-lr-design.md — colors, type, spacing, tokens>\\r\\n3. Content/pedagogy parity: <coaching tone, teach-first-calibrate-after gaps vs teaching-voice.md>\\r\\n4. Data/quality-bar gaps: <fake data, dead buttons, error handling — anything bootcamp-quality-bar.md flags>\\r\\n5. Verdict: <shipped-quality / in-progress / needs-work, one line, plus the single highest-leverage next fix>\\r\\n```\\r\\n\\r\\n## Rules\\r\\n\\r\\n- No em dashes. Terse per finding, don\'t pad with rationale unless asked.\\r\\n- Diagnosis only unless Joshua asks you to fix something. Report the delta, don\'t start building.\\r\\n- Don\'t re-read the full 216-file Intro to LR tree each time; use the entity/synthesis docs as the source of truth for what \\"done\\" means, and spot-check the codebase only where the docs are ambiguous.\\r\\n- If the target bootcamp has no entity page in `wiki/entities/`, flag that as a documentation gap in point 5 rather than silently skipping it.\\r\\n### handoff\\r\\n---\\r\\nname: handoff\\r\\ndescription: Compact the current conversation into a handoff document for another agent to pick up.\\r\\nargument-hint: \\"What will the next session be used for?\\"\\r\\ndisable-model-invocation: true\\r\\n---\\r\\n\\r\\nWrite a handoff document summarising the current conversation so a fresh agent can continue the work. Save to the temporary directory of the user\'s OS (`$TMPDIR`, else `/tmp`; `%TEMP%` on Windows) - not the current workspace.\\r\\n\\r\\nInclude a \\"suggested skills\\" section in the document, naming which skills the next agent should call the Skill tool for.\\r\\n\\r\\nDo not duplicate content already captured in other artifacts (specs, plans, ADRs, issues, commits, diffs). Reference them by path or URL instead.\\r\\n\\r\\nRedact any sensitive information, such as API keys, passwords, or personally identifiable information.\\r\\n\\r\\nIf the user passed arguments, treat them as a description of what the next session will focus on and tailor the doc accordingly.\\r\\n### brainstorming\\r\\n---\\r\\nname: brainstorming\\r\\ndescription: \\"You MUST use this before any creative work - creating features, building components, adding functionality, or modifying behavior. Explores user intent, requirements and design before implementation.\\"\\r\\n---\\r\\n\\r\\n# Brainstorming Ideas Into Designs\\r\\n\\r\\nHelp turn ideas into fully formed designs and specs through natural collaborative dialogue.\\r\\n\\r\\nStart by understanding the current project context, then ask questions one at a time to refine the idea. Once you understand what you\'re building, present the design and get user approval.\\r\\n\\r\\n<HARD-GATE>\\r\\nDo NOT invoke any implementation skill, write any code, scaffold any project, or take any implementation action until you have presented a design and the user has approved it. This applies to EVERY project regardless of perceived simplicity.\\r\\n</HARD-GATE>\\r\\n\\r\\n## Anti-Pattern: \\"This Is Too Simple To Need A Design\\"\\r\\n\\r\\nEvery project goes through this process. A todo list, a single-function utility, a config change — all of them. \\"Simple\\" projects are where unexamined assumptions cause the most wasted work. The design can be short (a few sentences for truly simple projects), but you MUST present it and get approval.\\r\\n\\r\\n## Checklist\\r\\n\\r\\nYou MUST create a task for each of these items and complete them in order:\\r\\n\\r\\n1. **Explore project context** — check files, docs, recent commits\\r\\n2. **Offer the visual companion just-in-time** — NOT upfront. The first time a question would genuinely be clearer shown than described, offer it then (its own message); on approval its browser tab opens for you. If no visual question ever arises, never offer it. See the Visual Companion section below.\\r\\n3. **Ask clarifying questions** — one at a time, understand purpose/constraints/success criteria\\r\\n4. **Propose 2-3 approaches** — with trade-offs and your recommendation\\r\\n5. **Present design** — in sections scaled to their complexity, get user approval after each section\\r\\n6. **Write design doc** — save to `docs/superpowers/specs/YYYY-MM-DD-<topic>-design.md` and commit\\r\\n7. **Spec self-review** — quick inline check for placeholders, contradictions, ambiguity, scope (see below)\\r\\n8. **User reviews written spec** — ask user to review the spec file before proceeding\\r\\n9. **Transition to implementation** — invoke writing-plans skill to create implementation plan\\r\\n\\r\\n## Process Flow\\r\\n\\r\\n```dot\\r\\ndigraph brainstorming {\\r\\n    \\"Explore project context\\" [shape=box];\\r\\n    \\"Ask clarifying questions\\" [shape=box];\\r\\n    \\"Propose 2-3 approaches\\" [shape=box];\\r\\n    \\"Present design sections\\" [shape=box];\\r\\n    \\"User approves design?\\" [shape=diamond];\\r\\n    \\"Write design doc\\" [shape=box];\\r\\n    \\"Spec self-review\\\\n(fix inline)\\" [shape=box];\\r\\n    \\"User reviews spec?\\" [shape=diamond];\\r\\n    \\"Invoke writing-plans skill\\" [shape=doublecircle];\\r\\n\\r\\n    \\"Explore project context\\" -> \\"Ask clarifying questions\\";\\r\\n    \\"Ask clarifying questions\\" -> \\"Propose 2-3 approaches\\";\\r\\n    \\"Propose 2-3 approaches\\" -> \\"Present design sections\\";\\r\\n    \\"Present design sections\\" -> \\"User approves design?\\";\\r\\n    \\"User approves design?\\" -> \\"Present design sections\\" [label=\\"no, revise\\"];\\r\\n    \\"User approves design?\\" -> \\"Write design doc\\" [label=\\"yes\\"];\\r\\n    \\"Write design doc\\" -> \\"Spec self-review\\\\n(fix inline)\\";\\r\\n    \\"Spec self-review\\\\n(fix inline)\\" -> \\"User reviews spec?\\";\\r\\n    \\"User reviews spec?\\" -> \\"Write design doc\\" [label=\\"changes requested\\"];\\r\\n    \\"User reviews spec?\\" -> \\"Invoke writing-plans skill\\" [label=\\"approved\\"];\\r\\n}\\r\\n```\\r\\n\\r\\n**The terminal state is invoking writing-plans.** Do NOT invoke frontend-design, mcp-builder, or any other implementation skill. The ONLY skill you invoke after brainstorming is writing-plans.\\r\\n\\r\\n## The Process\\r\\n\\r\\n**Understanding the idea:**\\r\\n### using-superpowers\\r\\n---\\r\\nname: using-superpowers\\r\\ndescription: Use when starting any conversation - establishes how to find and use skills, requiring skill invocation before ANY response including clarifying questions\\r\\n---\\r\\n\\r\\n<SUBAGENT-STOP>\\r\\nIf you were dispatched as a subagent to execute a specific task, ignore this skill.\\r\\n</SUBAGENT-STOP>\\r\\n\\r\\n<EXTREMELY-IMPORTANT>\\r\\nIf you think there is even a 1% chance a skill might apply to what you are doing, you ABSOLUTELY MUST invoke the skill.\\r\\n\\r\\nIF A SKILL APPLIES TO YOUR TASK, YOU DO NOT HAVE A CHOICE. YOU MUST USE IT.\\r\\n\\r\\nThis is not negotiable. You cannot rationalize your way out of this.\\r\\n</EXTREMELY-IMPORTANT>\\r\\n\\r\\n## The Rule\\r\\n\\r\\n**Invoke relevant or requested skills BEFORE any response or action** — including clarifying questions, exploring the codebase, or checking files. If it turns out wrong for the situation, you don\'t have to use it.\\r\\n\\r\\n**Before entering plan mode:** if you haven\'t already brainstormed, invoke the brainstorming skill first.\\r\\n\\r\\nThen announce \\"Using [skill] to [purpose]\\" and follow the skill exactly. If it has a checklist, create a todo per item.\\r\\n\\r\\n## Skill Priority\\r\\n\\r\\nWhen multiple skills apply, process skills come first — they set the approach, then implementation skills (frontend-design, etc.) carry it out. Brainstorming and systematic-debugging are Superpowers\' most common process skills, but the rule holds for any of them.\\r\\n\\r\\n- \\"Let\'s build X\\" → superpowers:brainstorming first, then implementation skills.\\r\\n- \\"Fix this bug\\" → superpowers:systematic-debugging first, then domain skills.\\r\\n\\r\\n## Red Flags\\r\\n\\r\\nThese thoughts mean STOP—you\'re rationalizing:\\r\\n\\r\\n| Thought | Reality |\\r\\n|---------|---------|\\r\\n| \\"This is just a simple question\\" | Questions are tasks. Check for skills. |\\r\\n| \\"I need more context first\\" | Skill check comes BEFORE clarifying questions. |\\r\\n| \\"Let me explore the codebase first\\" | Skills tell you HOW to explore. Check first. |\\r\\n| \\"I can check git/files quickly\\" | Files lack conversation context. Check for skills. |\\r\\n| \\"Let me gather information first\\" | Skills tell you HOW to gather information. |\\r\\n| \\"This doesn\'t need a formal skill\\" | If a skill exists, use it. |\\r\\n| \\"I remember this skill\\" | Skills evolve. Read current version. |\\r\\n| \\"This doesn\'t count as a task\\" | Action = task. Check for skills. |\\r\\n| \\"The skill is overkill\\" | Simple things become complex. Use it. |\\r\\n| \\"I\'ll just do this one thing first\\" | Check BEFORE doing anything. |\\r\\n| \\"This feels productive\\" | Undisciplined action wastes time. Skills prevent this. |\\r\\n| \\"I know what that means\\" | Knowing the concept ≠ using the skill. Invoke it. |\\r\\n\\r\\n## Platform Adaptation\\r\\n\\r\\nIf your harness appears here, read its reference file for special instructions:\\r\\n\\r\\n- Codex: `references/codex-tools.md`\\r\\n- Pi: `references/pi-tools.md`\\r\\n- Antigravity: `references/antigravity-tools.md`\\r\\n\\r\\n## User Instructions\\r\\n\\r\\nUser instructions (CLAUDE.md, AGENTS.md, GEMINI.md, etc, direct requests) take precedence over skills, which in turn override default behavior. Only skip skill workflows or instructions when your human partner has explicitly told you to.\\r\\n### send-booking-link\\r\\n---\\r\\nname: send-booking-link\\r\\ndescription: >\\r\\n  Draft the booking-link email to a student and log the follow-up loop. Use\\r\\n  when Joshua says \\"send <student> their booking link\\", \\"send booking links to\\r\\n  X, Y, Z\\", \\"get <student> scheduled\\", or asks who still needs one. Wraps the\\r\\n  lookup / draft / send / log pipeline that has been hand-orchestrated one\\r\\n  student at a time. Drafts by default; sends only on an explicit go-ahead.\\r\\nallowed-tools: Bash Read Write Edit Glob Grep\\r\\n---\\r\\n\\r\\n# Send booking link\\r\\n\\r\\nFour steps that were being done by hand, seven times in a single session:\\r\\nlook up the email, draft in Joshua\'s voice, send, log the open loop. This does\\r\\nall four, in order, for one student or a batch.\\r\\n\\r\\n## 1. Look up — never guess an address\\r\\n\\r\\nThe roster is generated; rebuild it first so it reflects current folders.\\r\\n\\r\\n```\\r\\npython3 system/scripts/build-roster.py\\r\\n```\\r\\n\\r\\nThen read `students/roster.generated.md` for the student\'s **email** and\\r\\n**booking link**. Both must be present before drafting.\\r\\n\\r\\n- **No email recorded** → stop. Do not guess, do not search for a plausible\\r\\n  address. Tell Joshua the student\'s page has no `email:` in frontmatter.\\r\\n- **No booking pass** → stop. The roster\'s \\"No booking pass\\" section lists\\r\\n  these. Booking access has to be granted before there is anything to send.\\r\\n- **Pass `exhausted`** → stop, and say so. The link is live but has no credits\\r\\n  left, so the student lands on \\"you\'ve used all your sessions\\". Sending it is\\r\\n  worse than sending nothing. Credits have to be added first.\\r\\n- **The URL slug is not the folder slug.** `yahunatan-zetvy` is\\r\\n  `/book/yahunathan`. Always read it from the roster; never derive it.\\r\\n- **Email disagrees with the backend** → stop and ask which is current. The\\r\\n  roster surfaces these rather than picking one.\\r\\n\\r\\nThe roster\'s booking columns are read **live** from `booking_passes` on every\\r\\nrebuild, so they are current as of the rebuild and revoked passes are already\\r\\nexcluded. That is why step 1 rebuilds first.\\r\\n\\r\\n## 2. Draft in Joshua\'s voice\\r\\n\\r\\nRoute through `wiki/teaching-voice.md`. This is student-facing copy, so the\\r\\nvoice rules are not optional.\\r\\n\\r\\nShape: short, warm, no overselling. Own any delay in the first line if there\\r\\nhas been one, give the real reason in a clause, move to the next step. Hand\\r\\nthem the link plainly. No em-dashes. No AI-slop vocabulary.\\r\\n\\r\\nPersonalize from the student\'s folder — `teaching-notes.md`, `open-loops.md`,\\r\\ntheir `<slug>.md` — so the email refers to where they actually are (what they\\r\\nwere last working on, what they said they wanted). A generic blast is the thing\\r\\nthis skill exists to avoid.\\r\\n\\r\\n## 3. Draft, then stop\\r\\n\\r\\n**Default is draft, not send.** Anything a student or prospect reads is drafted\\r\\nand never sent unless it is a pre-approved template and Joshua has said go.\\r\\n\\r\\nThe safety flag is `--draft`. It is the difference between a draft and a sent\\r\\nemail, so it is never omitted on the first pass.\\r\\n### teach\\r\\n---\\r\\nname: teach\\r\\ndescription: Teach the user a new skill or concept, within this workspace.\\r\\ndisable-model-invocation: true\\r\\nargument-hint: \\"What would you like to learn about?\\"\\r\\n---\\r\\n\\r\\nThe user has asked you to teach them something. This is a stateful request - they intend to learn the topic over multiple sessions.\\r\\n\\r\\n## Teaching Workspace\\r\\n\\r\\nTreat the current directory as a teaching workspace. Workspace paths (`./lessons/` and the rest) resolve from the directory `/teach` was run in; only the `*-FORMAT.md` links resolve from this skill\'s folder. The state of their learning is captured in this directory in several files:\\r\\n\\r\\n- `MISSION.md`: A document capturing the _reason_ the user is interested in the topic. This should be used to ground all teaching. Use the format in [MISSION-FORMAT.md](./MISSION-FORMAT.md).\\r\\n- `./reference/*.html`: A directory of reference materials. These are the compressed learnings from the lessons - cheat sheets, reference algorithms, syntax, yoga poses, glossaries. They are the raw units of learning. They should be beautiful documents which print out well, and are designed for quick reference.\\r\\n- `RESOURCES.md`: A list of resources which can be explored to ground your teaching in contextual knowledge, or to acquire knowledge and wisdom. Use the format in [RESOURCES-FORMAT.md](./RESOURCES-FORMAT.md).\\r\\n- `./learning-records/*.md`: A directory of learning records, which capture what the user has learned. These are loosely equivalent to architectural decision records in software development - they capture non-obvious lessons and key insights that may need to be revised later, or drive future sessions. These should be used to calculate the zone of proximal development. They are titled `0001-<dash-case-name>.md`, where the number increments each time. Use the format in [LEARNING-RECORD-FORMAT.md](./LEARNING-RECORD-FORMAT.md).\\r\\n- `./lessons/*.html`: A directory of lessons. A **lesson** is a single, self-contained HTML output that teaches one tightly-scoped thing tied to the mission. This is the primary unit of teaching in this workspace.\\r\\n- `./assets/*`: Reusable **components** shared across lessons. See [Assets](#assets).\\r\\n- `NOTES.md`: A scratchpad for you to jot down user preferences, or working notes.\\r\\n\\r\\n## Philosophy\\r\\n\\r\\nTo learn at a deep level, the user needs three things:\\r\\n\\r\\n- **Knowledge**, captured from high-quality, high-trust resources\\r\\n- **Skills**, acquired through highly-relevant interactive lessons devised by you, based on the knowledge\\r\\n- **Wisdom**, which comes from interacting with other learners and practitioners\\r\\n\\r\\nBefore the `RESOURCES.md` is well-populated, your focus should be to find high-quality resources which will help the user acquire knowledge. Never trust your parametric knowledge.\\r\\n\\r\\nSome topics may require more skills than knowledge. Learning more about theoretical physics might be more knowledge-based. For yoga, more skills-based.\\r\\n\\r\\n### Fluency vs Storage Strength\\r\\n\\r\\nYou should be careful to split between two types of learning:\\r\\n\\r\\n- **Fluency strength**: in-the-moment retrieval of knowledge\\r\\n- **Storage strength**: long-term retention of knowledge\\r\\n\\r\\nFluency can give the user an illusory sense of mastery, but storage strength is the real goal. Try to design lessons which build long-term retention by desirable difficulty:\\r\\n\\r\\n- Using retrieval practice (recall from memory)\\r\\n- Spacing (distributing practice over time)\\r\\n- Interleaving (mixing up different but related topics in practice - for skills practice only)\\r\\n\\r\\n## Lessons\\r\\n\\r\\nA lesson is the main thing you produce: the unit in which knowledge and skills reach the user. Each lesson is one self-contained HTML file, saved to `./lessons/` and titled `0001-<dash-case-name>.html` where the number increments each time.\\r\\n\\r\\nA lesson should be **beautiful**, with clean, readable typography and layout, since the user will return to these later to review. Think Tufte.\\r\\n\\r\\nThe lesson should be short, and completable very quickly. Learners\' working memory is very small, and we need to stay within it. But each lesson should give the user a single tangible win that they can build on. It should be directly tied to the mission, and should be in the user\'s zone of proximal development.\\r\\n\\r\\nIf possible, open the lesson file for the user by running a CLI command.\\r\\n\\r\\nEach lesson should link via HTML anchors to other lessons and reference documents.\\r\\n\\r\\nEach lesson should recommend a primary source for the user to read or watch. This should be the most high-quality, high-trust resource you found on the topic.\\r\\n\\r\\nEach lesson should contain a reminder to ask followup questions to the agent. The agent is their teacher, and can assist with anything that\'s unclear.\\r\\n\\r\\n## Assets\\r\\n\\r\\nLessons are built from reusable **components**, stored in `./assets/`: stylesheets, quiz widgets, simulators, diagram helpers, and anything else a second lesson could reuse.\\r\\n### tdd\\r\\n---\\r\\nname: tdd\\r\\ndescription: Test-driven development. Use when the user wants to build features or fix bugs test-first, mentions \\"red-green-refactor\\", or wants integration tests.\\r\\n---\\r\\n\\r\\n# Test-Driven Development\\r\\n\\r\\nTDD is the red → green loop. This skill is the reference that makes that loop produce tests worth keeping: what a good test is, where tests go, the anti-patterns, and the rules of the loop. Every section applies on every cycle: consult them before and during the loop, not after.\\r\\n\\r\\nWhen exploring the codebase, read `GLOSSARY.md` (if it exists) so test names and interface vocabulary match the project\'s domain language, and respect ADRs in the area you\'re touching.\\r\\n\\r\\n## What a good test is\\r\\n\\r\\nTests verify behavior through public interfaces, not implementation details. Code can change entirely; tests shouldn\'t. A good test reads like a specification: \\"user can checkout with valid cart\\" tells you exactly what capability exists, and it survives refactors because it doesn\'t care about internal structure.\\r\\n\\r\\nSee [tests.md](tests.md) for examples and [mocking.md](mocking.md) for mocking guidelines.\\r\\n\\r\\n## Seams: where tests go\\r\\n\\r\\nA **seam** is the public boundary you test at: the interface where you observe behavior without reaching inside. Tests live at seams, never against internals.\\r\\n\\r\\n**Test only at pre-agreed seams.** Before writing any test, write down the seams under test and confirm them with the user. No test is written at an unconfirmed seam. You can\'t test everything, so agreeing the seams up front is how testing effort lands on the critical paths and complex logic instead of every edge case.\\r\\n\\r\\nAsk: \\"What\'s the public interface, and which seams should we test?\\" Give each proposed seam a one-line note on what it catches and what it misses.\\r\\n\\r\\nWhen the shape of that interface is itself in question (how deep the module is, where the seam belongs, what the interface should expose), call the Skill tool with \\"codebase-design\\" for the vocabulary. It is the shared source of the module, interface, depth, seam, adapter, leverage and locality terms, and it is a reference to consult, not a session to run.\\r\\n\\r\\n## Anti-patterns\\r\\n\\r\\n- **Implementation-coupled**: mocks internal collaborators, tests private methods, or verifies through a side channel (querying the database instead of using the interface). The tell: the test breaks when you refactor but behavior hasn\'t changed.\\r\\n- **Tautological**: the assertion recomputes the expected value the way the code does (`expect(add(a, b)).toBe(a + b)`, a snapshot derived by hand the same way, a constant asserted equal to itself), so it passes by construction and can never disagree with the code. Expected values must come from an independent source of truth: a known-good literal, a worked example, the spec.\\r\\n- **Horizontal slicing**: writing all tests first, then all implementation. Bulk tests verify _imagined_ behavior: you test the _shape_ of things rather than user-facing behavior, the tests go insensitive to real changes, and you commit to test structure before understanding the implementation. Work in **vertical slices** instead: one test → one implementation → repeat, each test a **tracer bullet** that responds to what the last cycle taught you.\\r\\n\\r\\n## Rules of the loop\\r\\n\\r\\n- **Red before green.** Write the failing test first, then only enough code to pass it. Don\'t anticipate future tests or add speculative features.\\r\\n- **One slice at a time.** One seam, one test, one minimal implementation per cycle.\\r\\n- **Refactoring is not part of the loop.** It belongs to the review stage (see the `code-review` skill), not the red → green implementation cycle.\\r\\n"}'}]

[{'type': 'input_text', 'text': 'Script completed\nWall time 8.2 seconds\nOutput:\n'}, {'type': 'input_text', 'text': 'Warning: truncated output (original token count: 13360)\nTotal output lines: 1\n\n{"chunk_id":"4cf438","wall_time_seconds":1.090852,"exit_code":0,"original_token_count":17401,"output":"Warning: truncated output (original token count: 17401)\\nTotal output lines: 802\\n\\n### assign-lsatu-work\\r\\n---\\r\\nname: assign-lsatu-work\\r\\ndescription: Operate LSAT U headlessly. Assign guided drills and daily schedules through a mapped catalog and verified batch MCP; assign activities or timed sections, read student progress, manage access and Classroom work, and handle platform messages.\\r\\n---\\r\\n\\r\\n# Assign LSAT U work\\r\\n\\r\\nFor guided-drill selection or schedules, follow [the guided-drill workflow](references/guided-drill-workflow.md). Use the mapped catalog, one live preview and one batch MCP assignment. This local branch contains its authorization and verification rules; do not load the global reference for a routine guided schedule.\\r\\n\\r\\nThis is a pointer. The full skill lives in ONE place:\\r\\n\\r\\n    C:\\\\Users\\\\Joshu\\\\.agents\\\\skills\\\\assign-lsatu-work\\\\SKILL.md\\r\\n    (identical to C:\\\\Users\\\\Joshu\\\\.claude\\\\skills\\\\assign-lsatu-work\\\\SKILL.md, which Claude uses)\\r\\n\\r\\nFor other LSAT U operations, read that file in full and follow it exactly.\\r\\nDo not copy its contents here; this file must stay a pointer so the two runtimes never drift.\\r\\n\\r\\nThe short version, in case the file cannot be read:\\r\\n\\r\\n- Every LSAT U operation runs headless through ONE command, from the vault root, with bash:\\r\\n  `bash system/scripts/lsatu <command> ...`\\r\\n  Examples: `bash system/scripts/lsatu status \\"Celia\\"`,\\r\\n  `bash system/scripts/lsatu assign --student \\"Celia\\" --section PT156.S2 --due 2026-09-30`.\\r\\n- No browser, no Chrome, no Lovable for routine content or assignments. Use\\r\\n  `lsat-u-platform-actions` for a complete interactive Classroom lesson: its\\r\\n  local MCP posts the HTML directly and verifies the saved copy headlessly.\\r\\n  This skill handles other assignments and student operations.\\r\\n- Reads never need permission. One named student assign / message: run it, then report.\\r\\n  Confirm first: 3+ students, revoke/archive/unarchive/unassign/all-off, unsend.\\r\\n- Never pass a multi-line argument. On Windows a newline drops `--dry-run` and sends for real\\r\\n  (this happened on 2026-09-23). The wrapper refuses it; do not work around it.\\r\\n\\r\\nGuided-drill catalog and MCP details live in the [guided workflow reference](references/guided-drill-workflow.md), including the authored-content exception and immediate fallback when new MCP tools have not appeared in a chat yet.\\r\\n### audit\\r\\n---\\r\\nname: audit\\r\\ndescription: Use when someone asks to audit their AIOS, score the Four Cs, find stale paths or unlinked projects, compare AGENTS.md and CLAUDE.md, check Claude/Codex skill compatibility, or assess migration readiness. Automatically saves dated reports and tracks evidence-backed improvements across runs.\\r\\n---\\r\\n\\r\\n# AIOS Audit\\r\\n\\r\\nCheck whether this AIOS can find the right information and do useful work reliably, and identify changes that would make the user\'s work easier. Score **Context, Connections, Capabilities, and Cadence out of 25 each**, using [rubric.md](rubric.md). This is rubric **v2**. Label the number **verified operational reliability**, not overall usefulness or percentage of work the AIOS can do. A folder, installed skill, API key, or confident claim is not proof of a working system.\\r\\n\\r\\nRun locally in the current project. Do not launch subagents unless the user requests them. Audit first; `/link` repairs a route, and `/level-up` helps close one meaningful gap. Never inflate or deliberately depress a score to encourage another run. Improvement comes from better evidence and behavior.\\r\\n\\r\\n**Every audit automatically saves its report in the audited project\'s `audits/` folder.** Read [history.md](history.md) for prior-report selection, finding transitions, comparison rules, and safe persistence. Saving the local audit record is part of this skill, not a separate approval step. An explicit user request not to save overrides this default. The inspected system remains unchanged.\\r\\n\\r\\n## 1. Establish scope and evidence\\r\\n\\r\\n- Get the current date and project root. Read applicable `AGENTS.md`, `CLAUDE.md`, and local overrides; follow the runtime\'s instruction hierarchy. Read both manuals when both exist. Check for conflicting routing and promised synchronization, without assuming distinct runtime instructions must be identical.\\r\\n- Load the relevant prior AIOS report and carried finding ledger using [history.md](history.md), before selecting probes. Recheck important prior findings alongside current priorities; do not assume earlier results remain true. Identify the comparison baseline and scope changes before scoring.\\r\\n- Use the manual\'s routing rules first. Read its project and knowledge indexes before listing their immediate child folders. Inspect only relevant scoped manuals. Skip dependencies, caches, generated output, and archives unless a route points there or an archived/current ambiguity needs checking.\\r\\n- Identify the user\'s role, main objective, current priorities, and up to three important workflows from actual context. Unfilled template placeholders do not count. Do not require business revenue data from someone whose work has no revenue function.\\r\\n- Inspect the supported skill/agent registries, connection references, and actual scheduler configuration/run evidence. Accept scripts, MCPs, exports, local data, and equivalent mechanisms equally. Count inventories for orientation only.\\r\\n- Record each finding as **verified**, **documented but unverified**, **missing**, **stale**, or **conflicting**, with a file/line, source URL, or dated run reference. File modification times and last-checked labels alone do not prove a successful refresh or execution.\\r\\n- Start with targeted reads. If a time budget or local page limit prevents verification, mark it unverified and state coverage. Never award full points because there was no time to check. Do not claim an exhaustive audit from a sample.\\r\\n\\r\\n## 2. Test routing and context retrieval\\r\\n\\r\\nMake a compact map: **user need → manual/index → specific source → freshness rule**. Include applicable business context, people, priorities/commitments, original records, project deliverables, specialist knowledge bases, media/assets, and external systems. A generic folder or provider name is insufficient when it leaves the relevant source unclear.\\r\\n\\r\\nCompare the maps with immediate folders to find important unindexed projects, outdated counts, broken paths, ambiguous aliases, duplicate sources of truth, and retired material presented as active. Distinguish confirmed gaps from folders whose relevance is unknown. Check whether supplied routes work from the current checkout, including references inside skills and generated mirrors where that runtime uses them.\\r\\n\\r\\nFollow the declared routes for these five questions, adapted to the user\'s real work:\\r\\n\\r\\n1. What does this person/business do, for whom, and what matters now?\\r\\n2. Where is the authoritative current priority, commitment, or status, and how would I verify it?\\r\\n3. Where is the latest deliverable and next step for an important active project?\\r\\n4. Where is a previous decision, lesson, or subject-specific knowledge item and its supporting source?\\r\\n5. Where is one commonly needed external record, asset, or original document, and how is it accessed?\\r\\n\\r\\nSelect relevant examples before searching for answers. If a category does not apply, record why and substitute a different real retrieval need, keeping five probes. For each, show the question, route attempted, source, result, and whether it was found directly, only by fallback search, or not found. A broad search can recover an answer, but it does not prove the declared route works. Mark external access unverified if not checked; a documented access path earns only documentation credit. Score only the evidence actually observed.\\r\\n\\r\\n**Check freshness and authority explicitly:**\\r\\n\\r\\n- An optional `_hot.md`, briefing, or cache earns no points just for existing. Do not recommend creating one by default. Check whether it duplicates canonical pages, has a real refresh mechanism, and presents stale numbers or past deadlines as current. A recently edited header does not refresh every fact inside it.\\r\\n- If a cache adds duplication without reliable upkeep, recommend bypassing it in retrieval and using the relevant index/source directly. Never automatically remove it. No cache is a valid architecture.\\r\\n- Stable context can live in a wiki; current metrics and task status should resolve to the appropriate live system or dated export. Exact terms should resolve to original records. Check source dates and flag conflicts rather than treating the wiki as automatically authoritative for every type of fact.\\r\\n- Check whether a fresh session could understand the user, resume the selected project, and find evidence without depending on this conversation. Praise compact, accurate routing; do not reward manual length, exhaustive root catalogs, or reading every wiki page.\\r\\n\\r\\n## 3. Verify the other three Cs\\r\\n\\r\\nFirst run the required [routing and cross-runtime compatibility checks](compatibility.md). This covers stale/broken paths, important unlinked work, differences between operating manuals, and skill availability across the runtimes in use or targeted for migration. Compare shared behavior and required resources, not raw file equality alone. Record expected runtime differences separately from defects. The protocol also defines the mandatory compatibility table, evidence labels, and calibration cases.\\r\\n\\r\\n**Connections:** Identify applicable domains: finances, customer interactions, calendar, communication, tasks, meetings, and knowledge/files; add content or specialist domains when material. Record each domain\'s relevance, mechanism, specific access route, successful-read evidence, date, and limitations. One tool may cover multiple domains only when each has evidence. A configured MCP or `.env` key does not establish authentication. Use narrow, safe read-only checks when available, or dated successful-run evidence within the source\'s expected refresh interval. With no documented interval, use 30 days and explain why highly volatile data may require a fresh read. Do not print secret values or bulk private records. Do not run unknown scripts before checking their side effects.\\r\\n\\r\\n**Capabilities:** Select up to three workflows tied to the identified priorities, not merely the most polished demos. Examine triggers, inputs, output destination, examples of actual usable outputs, verification, failure handling, and repeated use. Missing workflows remain gaps. Check discoverability, needed supporting files, and canonical/mirror consistency after documented transforms. Agents are optional; quantity, complexity, and custom naming earn no bonus. Use existing outputs or safe bounded checks; do not start paid generation or substantive work just to audit it.\\r\\n\\r\\n**Cadence:** Inspect actual enabled schedules, event triggers, hooks, or explicitly defined human-run rituals and their execution records. Identify the host/runtime, trigger, expected output, last due execution, success/failure evidence, and stop/recovery controls. A skill named `daily-*`, a template, or recently edited files does not establish cadence. A useful manual ritual gets limited credit; label it manual. Do not call a local job unattended or laptop-independent without evidence for that environment. Judge monthly or quarterly routines against their real due dates rather than a fixed weekly window.\\r\\n\\r\\n## 4. Score and prioritize\\r\\n\\r\\nRead the complete [rubric.md](rubric.md). Assign all 20 criterion scores, then apply its caps. Show the four subtotals, raw sum, any cap and reason, final score, and stage. Missing evidence earns no verified credit, but distinguish **unverified** from **known broken**. Record excluded domains with reasons; do not exclude a domain merely because it is disconnected.\\r\\n\\r\\nRank gaps by likely effect on the user\'s work, with wrong/stale answers and missing source access ahead of cosmetic tidiness. Give up to three concrete fixes with an exact affected route/workflow, supporting evidence, and a clear completion check. Do not invent three faults in a healthy system. Distinguish a repair from a check needed to resolve uncertainty.\\r\\n\\r\\nGroup findings into **confirmed defects**, **verification gaps**, and **improvement opportunities**; list intentional differences separately. Keep severity distinct from confidence. Assign each underlying issue a stable ID and reuse it across sections. Do not count one missing mirror or bad route as multiple independent defects. State which existing rubric criteria it affects; do not introduce a migration score or change the v2 anchors. Explain score limitations, including manual-cadence limits when relevant. Unchecked evidence is not proof of failure, and optional enhancements are not defects merely because they are absent.\\r\\n\\r\\n## 5. Return a concise, reviewable report\\r\\n\\r\\nUse this structure, keeping the evidence ledger compact:\\r\\n\\r\\n1. **AIOS Audit: date, project, rubric v2.** Scope, runtimes, verification limits, and a plain-language conclusion. Lead with what works and the most consequential mismatch. Report unique finding counts by class, not as an exhaustive total outside the inspected scope.\\r\\n2. **AGENTS.md / CLAUDE.md findings:** always include the dedicated section specified below, even when no issues are found. Do not bury operating-manual findings in the general fixes or routing table.\\r\\n3. **Routing and migration compatibility:** the coverage/matrix and actionable findings from [compatibility.md](compatibility.md), including confirmed defects, verification gaps, intentional differences, and improvement opportunities. Reference existing finding IDs instead of repeating full manual findings. State whether sampled migration is blocked, needs verification, or passed the inspected checks; do not imply the whole system is portable from a sample.\\r\\n4. **Routing check:** five probe results, including source references and direct/fallback/unresolved status.\\r\\n5. **What works:** up to three evidence-backed strengths.\\r\\n6. **Verified operational reliability:** four rows, each `/25`; raw total, caps, final `/100`, and stage. Include criterion IDs and awarded points so arithmetic is reproducible. Explain separately how confirmed defects and unverified evidence limited credit. This is not an overall usefulness grade.\\r\\n7. **Top improvements:** up to three ranked actions, each labeled repair, verify, or optional improvement, with evidence, exact next action, expected practical benefit, and what would prove it complete. Refer to finding IDs instead of repeating them in full.\\r\\n8. **Progress since the previous audit:** link the baseline, show finding transitions and evidence from [history.md](history.md), and explain any comparable score change. Separate actual repairs, newly verified evidence, regressions, and coverage/rubric changes. No prior comparable report means a new baseline, not an invented improvement.\\r\\n9. **Next run:** a ready-to-use `/level-up` prompt carrying the highest-value gap, evidence, and acceptance check; use `/link <target> <purpose>` for a routing-only fix. Recommend these commands only if installed; otherwise give the equivalent plain-language task. `/grill-me`, if available, is useful for genuinely missing context, not for facts already stored elsewhere.\\r\\n10. **Saved record:** write and read back the complete report using [templates/report.md](templates/report.md). Link the actual saved file in the final reply. The chat can be concise; the saved record must retain the score breakdown, evidence, compatibility checks, and carried finding ledger. Never say saved without confirming it.\\r\\n\\r\\n### Required section: AGENTS.md / CLAUDE.md findings\\r\\n\\r\\nStart by naming the exact root manuals inspected and the scoped manuals sampled. Mark each root manual **checked**, **missing**, or **not checked**, with a reason where needed. State whether their shared guidance agrees, conflicts, or intentionally differs. Do not imply that inspecting one file verifies the other; a setup with only one applicable manual does not need a duplicate merely to pass.\\r\\n\\r\\nThen show a compact findings table:\\r\\n\\r\\n| File and section/line | Rule or missing route | Finding and practical effect | Recommended change |\\r\\n|---|---|---|---|\\r\\n| Exact clickable file reference | Short quote or precise paraphrase; label omissions explicitly | What was verified, stale, conflicting, broken, or unverified, and how that affects finding or using information | Specific edit or verification step |\\r\\n\\r\\nSeparate **problems in the manual itself** from **problems in files it routes to**. For example, a stale target index is a downstream maintenance gap unless the manual also directs readers to the wrong index. Name the downstream file and the route that reaches it. Include one brief statement about what the manuals already do well. If no issues are found, explicitly say \\"No operating-manual issues found in the inspected scope\\" and state any coverage limits; do not invent findings to fill the table.\\r\\n\\r\\nFinish the section with whether any manuals were changed. In a standard read-only audit, say **\\"No operating manuals were changed.\\"** These findings inform the existing Four-Cs criteria and caps; do not add a fifth score or double-count deductions. Apply this section to both chat reports and saved reports.\\r\\n\\r\\nRecommend rerunning `/audit` after the selected fix and weekly during active setup, then at a sensible maintenance interval. Compare with a previous saved report only when scope and rubric match; v1 scores need a new baseline. Scores can decrease when evidence becomes stale. Do not promise a higher score from another run alone.\\r\\n\\r\\nThe audit is read-only toward inspected systems: no repairs, file moves, installation, scheduler changes, messages, or external writes. Its sole default write is a new local audit report under `audits/` (create the directory if needed). Preserve earlier reports, redact secrets and unnecessary private records, and do not update business memory or source-of-truth files from audit observations. On an incomplete run, save a clearly marked partial report when possible; do not present it as a completed audit or fabricate a score. If saving fails, report that explicitly and return the report in chat.\\r\\n### booking-link\\r\\n---\\r\\nname: booking-link\\r\\ndescription: Use whenever Joshua wants a one-off booking link for LSAT U — \\"make me a link for Dakota at 7:15 tomorrow\\", \\"send her a link to book tonight\\", \\"one-off link, $60\\", \\"short notice link\\", \\"I need a link she can schedule herself with\\". Mints a single-use URL that sells exactly one session at a price you set, optionally pinned to one exact time, and closes after she books. Also covers listing and revoking existing links.\\r\\n---\\r\\n\\r\\n# One-off booking links\\r\\n\\r\\nA URL Joshua sends to one person. She opens it, books one session, pays, and\\r\\ngets the Google Meet invite from the ordinary booking flow. Then the link\\r\\ncloses.\\r\\n\\r\\n## Authorization\\r\\n\\r\\nMinting a link is pre-authorized. Joshua asking for a link means make it now —\\r\\ndo not ask permission, ask only for the facts you actually need.\\r\\n\\r\\n**Never send the link anywhere.** Print it and hand it to Joshua. He decides who\\r\\ngets it. A link is a Bearer [REDACTED]: whoever holds it can book that slot.\\r\\n\\r\\n## What you need before running\\r\\n\\r\\nOnly two things are required, and one has a default:\\r\\n\\r\\n- **Price** in dollars. Required — links always charge, and the standard rate is\\r\\n  $45 but a given person may pay something else. Ask if it was not said.\\r\\n- **Who it is for.** Used only …3360 tokens truncated…onstraints. Consider ambiguity, code dependencies, verification difficulty, context size, and cost or speed preferences. A short prompt can describe a difficult task. Preserve explicit model and provider choices; do not silently replace them with your preferred pairing.\\r\\n\\r\\nTreat a request for advice as recommendation-only. A request to route and perform work authorizes the scoped handoff within the user\'s existing permissions. The skill invocation by itself does not authorize implementation. Ask a question only when a missing fact materially changes the recommendation or authorized work; otherwise state your assumption.\\r\\n\\r\\n## Choose the role before the model\\r\\n\\r\\n| Situation | Useful next step |\\r\\n|---|---|\\r\\n| Straightforward task, sufficient context, no reason to delegate | Stay with the current agent; avoid handoff overhead |\\r\\n| A consequential or ambiguous plan is ready | Ask another provider to challenge requirements, assumptions, and acceptance criteria before building |\\r\\n| An implementation is ready | Ask another provider to inspect relevant changes against requirements, including test validity |\\r\\n| Repeated attempts have failed | Give another provider the reproduction, evidence, and failed approaches; ask for a testable alternative explanation |\\r\\n| A separable task has clear inputs and acceptance checks | Delegate that piece to a suitable smaller model and inspect its result |\\r\\n| The user wants repeated planning, revision, building, and independent inspection | Recommend Claudex Loop; load that separate skill only if the user requests that workflow |\\r\\n\\r\\nThe current agent keeps the user\'s requirements and coordinates the work. A different provider offers another perspective, not guaranteed correctness. A cheaper delegate does not need to be a peer reviewer of the entire architecture.\\r\\n\\r\\n## Select a practical candidate\\r\\n\\r\\nStart with models available in the user\'s environment. The following are dated starting points (September 2026), not a permanent leaderboard:\\r\\n\\r\\n- **GPT-5.6 Luna** (`gpt-5.6-luna`): consider for narrow, repetitive tasks with explicit checks, such as fixtures, extraction, documentation updates, or an isolated helper.\\r\\n- **GPT-5.6 Terra** (`gpt-5.6-terra`): consider for bounded coding or investigation requiring more judgment and context than the Luna task above.\\r\\n- **GPT-6 Astra** (`gpt-6-astra`) and **Claude Fable 5.1** (`claude-fable-5-1`): candidates for ambiguous work, difficult debugging, or a substantial independent review. From Codex, Fable is a candidate for cross-provider review; from Claude Code, Astra is a candidate.\\r\\n- **Claude Sonnet, Opus, or another available model**: retain as options when their task fit, existing context, account access, or the user\'s preference favors them. Cross-provider delegation is optional.\\r\\n\\r\\nUse local model listings and CLI status/help when accessible without launching a model task. Distinguish listed, authenticated, and proven runnable: none alone establishes the others. If access or the active model is unknown, make the recommendation conditional and explain what needs checking. Do not launch paid comparison calls just to choose a model.\\r\\n\\r\\nFor price-sensitive choices or comparative claims, consult current official [OpenAI model information](https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/models) and [Anthropic model information](https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/about-claude/models/overview). Check [Codex usage guidance](https://learn.chatgpt.com/docs/pricing) when using subscription allowances. API token prices are different from subscription usage; task costs also include context transfer, reasoning, retries, and host verification. Do not call Terra cheaper than Sonnet, claim Luna is universally stronger, or promise savings without relevant evidence. If sources cannot be checked, omit numeric claims and label the cost assumption.\\r\\n\\r\\n## Return a short routing brief\\r\\n\\r\\nNormally use fewer than 200 words:\\r\\n\\r\\n- **Recommendation:** stay here or use a named provider/model for a specific role.\\r\\n- **Why:** one or two reasons tied to this task, plus a material uncertainty if present.\\r\\n- **Handoff:** the bounded assignment, relevant context/files, expected result, permitted actions, and how to check success. If staying here, give the immediate next step instead.\\r\\n\\r\\nOffer at most one alternative when it helps a real tradeoff. Do not interview the user, generate a catalog of models, or start a plan-review loop. Do not claim to have changed the current session\'s model; a child CLI invocation is a separate session.\\r\\n\\r\\n## Execute one handoff when requested\\r\\n\\r\\nUse the selected provider\'s CLI from the correct project directory, explicitly selecting the recommended or requested model for that call. Check the actual binary\'s version and help; consult the relevant official [Codex non-interactive guide](https://learn.chatgpt.com/docs/non-interactive-mode) or [Claude programmatic guide](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/headless) if needed. Avoid changing global defaults, installing software, or switching models silently to make a call succeed.\\r\\n\\r\\nPass a self-contained brief with the goal, relevant requirements and files, constraints, expected output, and verification. For debugging, include failed attempts. For code inspection, identify the comparison baseline and relevant committed, staged, unstaged, and untracked changes. The child does not inherit the conversation. Send prompt text through stdin or a safely handled file; never interpolate arbitrary prompts into shell commands.\\r\\n\\r\\nFor review or diagnosis, use supported read-only project tools and restrict external write-capable tools too; a prompt saying \\"read-only\\" is not enforcement. If those restrictions cannot be established, return the prepared handoff and explain the limitation. For authorized edits, use scoped write permissions and preserve existing user changes; use an isolated worktree when concurrent edits would conflict. Never bypass permissions. The host pauses edits to the delegate\'s files while it works.\\r\\n\\r\\nUse a fresh session for the one-off handoff, a bounded timeout, and separate stdout/stderr artifacts in a unique temporary directory outside the project. Keep the user informed during long calls. Read the completed result and exit status; an empty response, timeout, or permission failure is not success. Stop and report a failed handoff rather than automatically retrying, escalating to a larger model, or starting another round. If a timed-out process may still run, resolve its status before restarting work on the same files.\\r\\n\\r\\nAssess findings against evidence, inspect any edits, and run appropriate checks within existing authorization. Report the outcome, checks actually run, and remaining uncertainty. Distinguish the model requested from the model observed; do not invent an observed identity. If a correction is outside the requested work, recommend it without expanding scope. Finish after this handoff and host verification; further delegation follows the user\'s request.\\r\\n### codex-build\\r\\n---\\r\\nname: codex-build\\r\\ndescription: \\"Claude-host entry point: Codex handles independent review or scoped delegation. Have Codex implement a concrete work order and have Claude independently inspect the final changes. Claude then inspects all changes and independently runs proof checks. Log evidence and limitations. A fresh Claude CLI inspector is also available through the shared runner if useful.\\r\\n- In Codex, implement in the current host session with its normal tools, then use a fresh Claude inspector through `inspect --host codex --builder codex`. If the spec still needs consequential decisions, settle those before delegating; do not build by inventing missing requirements.\\r\\n\\r\\nPreserve unrelated changes, record the baseline, independently run the proof, inspect staged and new files as well as the unstaged diff, and keep fix rounds bounded. After a Claude takeover, require fresh Codex inspection of Claude\'s edits; if both contributed, log authorship and have each inspect the other\'s changes. Never present an earlier review as covering later fixes. Present the completed diff for any remaining sign-off required by the user\'s authorization.\\r\\n### codex-review\\r\\n---\\r\\nname: codex-review\\r\\ndescription: \\"Claude-host entry point: Codex handles independent review or scoped delegation. Have Codex independently review an existing implementation plan while Claude coordinates a bounded revision loop. The shared workflow and executable live in the sibling `claudex-loop` skill; install that skill alongside this one.\\r\\n\\r\\nIn Claude Code, load [claudex-loop](../claudex-loop/SKILL.md) and start at `mode=review`, `host=claude`, reviewer Codex. An independent plan review does not replace independent review of the final code.\\r\\n### consultation-followup-drafts\\r\\n---\\r\\nname: consultation-followup-drafts\\r\\ndescription: \\"Daily: detect past consultations with Gemini notes and draft (not send) personalized follow-up emails from the transcript\\"\\r\\n---\\r\\n\\r\\nYou are Joshua\'s email drafting partner for aspiringattorneys.com (LSAT tutoring). Only create Gmail drafts.\\r\\n\\r\\nSTEP 1 — Read voice + template (required):\\r\\n- Read C:/Users/Joshu/dev/ai-os/wiki/CONSULTATION-FOLLOW-UP-TEMPLATE.md (the real template, rebuilt 2026-09-11 from sent mail; the old PDF and archive paths are retired)\\r\\n- Read C:/Users/Joshu/dev/ai-os/wiki/teaching-voice.md\\r\\nUse the template body verbatim. Create it with `gws gmail users drafts create` (raw RFC822, base64url), replying in the existing thread (threadId + In-Reply-To) if one exists, otherwise a new draft with subject \\"Next steps + tutoring options\\". Do NOT send.\\r\\n\\r\\nSTEP 6 — Report: for each consultation, the student\'s name/email, the detail you mirrored, which variant you used, and that a draft is waiting in Gmail for review. If no consultations were ready, say so in one line. Flag anything uncertain (e.g. couldn\'t tell if they already booked) so Joshua can check before sending.\\r\\n### consultation-inquiry-drafts\\r\\n---\\r\\nname: consultation-inquiry-drafts\\r\\ndescription: \\"Daily sweep: draft, but do not send, personalized consultation-link replies to new LSAT tutoring inquiries\\"\\r\\n---\\r\\n\\r\\n# Consultation Inquiry Drafts\\r\\n\\r\\nFind new LSAT tutoring inquiries and prepare Gmail drafts for Joshua to review. Never send. AI-generated replies remain drafts unless Joshua separately approves the exact message.\\r\\n\\r\\n## Required context\\r\\n\\r\\nBefore drafting:\\r\\n\\r\\n1. Read `C:/Users/Joshu/dev/ai-os/wiki/teaching-voice.md`.\\r\\n2. Read `C:/Users/Joshu/dev/ai-os/context/work.md` for current offers, booking, and billing rules.\\r\\n3. Use Gmail only through the `gws` CLI. Do not use Google connector MCPs.\\r\\n4. If the sender may already be a student, check `students/<name>/` first. Use Gmail and other live systems only when the student file does not resolve identity or current state.\\r\\n\\r\\n## Find eligible inquiries\\r\\n\\r\\nSearch Gmail for recent inbox threads that appear to be genuine new tutoring inquiries. A useful starting query is:\\r\\n\\r\\n```text\\r\\nin:inbox newer_than:2d -in:sent\\r\\n```\\r\\n\\r\\nInclude people asking about tutoring, rates, availability, consultations, referrals, or how to begin.\\r\\n\\r\\nSkip:\\r\\n\\r\\n- Existing-student logistics.\\r\\n- Booking and calendar notifications.\\r\\n- Newsletters and spam.\\r\\n- Any thread Joshua has already answered.\\r\\n- Anyone who has already paid or moved past consultation. Route those cases according to their actual student and payment state.\\r\\n\\r\\nUnread status is a clue, not proof that a reply is owed. Inspect the thread and confirm Joshua has not already responded.\\r\\n\\r\\n## Drafting rules\\r\\n\\r\\nEach reply must:\\r\\n\\r\\n- React to at least one real detail from the inquiry, such as a score, test date, platform, referral, plateau, or specific struggle.\\r\\n- Use a brief general acknowledgment only when the inquiry contains no useful detail.\\r\\n- Invite the prospect to a free consultation using `https://cal.com/joshua-jtx5ud/consultation`.\\r\\n- Explain the consultation in one short, low-pressure sentence.\\r\\n- Mention the current rate, `$40/h`, only when the person asks about price, rates, cost, or affordability.\\r\\n- Use a brief apology near the opening when Joshua\'s reply is more than about 24 hours late.\\r\\n- Stay under roughly 120 words, unless the inquiry genuinely requires more.\\r\\n- Use prose only, no bullets and no em dashes.\\r\\n- Default to `Hi [First name],` and `Best,\\\\nJoshua`. Use `Hey` only when the sender\'s tone and relationship clearly support it.\\r\\n- Invite the person to reply if the booking link does not work.\\r\\n\\r\\nDo not copy canned situation lines blindly. Mirror the person\'s message in natural language and follow the current teaching-voice page.\\r\\n\\r\\n## Gmail draft behavior\\r\\n\\r\\nCreate the draft through `gws`. Reply inside the existing Gmail thread whenever one exists. Preserve the thread context and reply headers rather than starting a new conversation. Do not send.\\r\\n\\r\\n## Report and log\\r\\n\\r\\nReport each prospect\'s name, email, the detail mirrored, and that a Gmail draft is waiting for review. Flag uncertain identity, prior-contact, pricing, or student-status cases.\\r\\n\\r\\nAppend each created draft to `wiki/send-ledger.md` with status `drafted`. Gmail remains the authority for whether anything was actually sent.\\r\\n### defuddle\\r\\n---\\r\\nname: defuddle\\r\\ndescription: Extract clean markdown content from web pages using Defuddle CLI, removing clutter and navigation to save tokens. Use instead of WebFetch when the user provides a URL to read or analyze, for online documentation, articles, blog posts, or any standard web page. Do NOT use for URLs ending in .md — those are already markdown, use WebFetch directly.\\r\\n---\\r\\n\\r\\n# Defuddle\\r\\n\\r\\nUse Defuddle CLI to extract clean readable content from web pages. Prefer over WebFetch for standard web pages — it removes navigation, ads, and clutter, reducing token usage.\\r\\n\\r\\nIf not installed: `npm install -g defuddle`\\r\\n\\r\\n## Usage\\r\\n\\r\\nAlways use `--md` for markdown output:\\r\\n\\r\\n```bash\\r\\ndefuddle parse <url> --md\\r\\n```\\r\\n\\r\\nSave to file:\\r\\n\\r\\n```bash\\r\\ndefuddle parse <url> --md -o content.md\\r\\n```\\r\\n\\r\\nExtract specific metadata:\\r\\n\\r\\n```bash\\r\\ndefuddle parse <url> -p title\\r\\ndefuddle parse <url> -p description\\r\\ndefuddle parse <url> -p domain\\r\\n```\\r\\n\\r\\n## Output formats\\r\\n\\r\\n| Flag | Format |\\r\\n|------|--------|\\r\\n| `--md` | Markdown (default choice) |\\r\\n| `--json` | JSON with both HTML and markdown |\\r\\n| (none) | HTML |\\r\\n| `-p <name>` | Specific metadata property |\\r\\n"}'}]
