Only events with an eventType of default may be imported.\\r\\nDeprecated behavior: If a non-default event is imported, its type will be changed to default and any event-type-specific properties it may have will be dropped.\\r\\n  - `insert` — Creates an event.\\r\\n  - `instances` — Returns instances of the specified recurring event.\\r\\n  - `list` — Returns events on the specified calendar.\\r\\n  - `move` — Moves an event to another calendar, i.e. changes an event\'s organizer. Note that only default events can be moved; birthday, focusTime, fromGmail, outOfOffice and workingLocation events cannot be moved.\\r\\n  - `patch` — Updates an event. This method supports patch semantics.\\r\\n  - `quickAdd` — Creates an event based on a simple text string.\\r\\n  - `update` — Updates an event.\\r\\n  - `watch` — Watch for changes to Events resources.\\r\\n\\r\\n### freebusy\\r\\n\\r\\n  - `query` — Returns free/busy information for a set of calendars.\\r\\n\\r\\n### settings\\r\\n\\r\\n  - `get` — Returns a single user setting.\\r\\n  - `list` — Returns all user settings for the authenticated user.\\r\\n  - `watch` — Watch for changes to Settings resources.\\r\\n\\r\\n## Discovering Commands\\r\\n\\r\\nBefore calling any API method, inspect it:\\r\\n\\r\\n```bash\\r\\n# Browse resources and methods\\r\\ngws calendar --help\\r\\n\\r\\n# Inspect a method\'s required params, types, and defaults\\r\\ngws schema calendar.<resource>.<method>\\r\\n```\\r\\n\\r\\nUse `gws schema` output to build your `--params` and `--json` flags.\\r\\n\\r\\n### gws-calendar-agenda\\r\\n---\\r\\nname: gws-calendar-agenda\\r\\ndescription: \\"Google Calendar: Show upcoming events across all calendars.\\"\\r\\nmetadata:\\r\\n  version: 0.22.1\\r\\n  openclaw:\\r\\n    category: \\"productivity\\"\\r\\n    requires:\\r\\n      bins:\\r\\n        - gws\\r\\n    cliHelp: \\"gws calendar +agenda --help\\"\\r\\n---\\r\\n\\r\\n# calendar +agenda\\r\\n\\r\\n> **PREREQUISITE:** Read `../gws-shared/SKILL.md` for auth, global flags, and security rules. If missing, run `gws generate-skills` to create it.\\r\\n\\r\\nShow upcoming events across all calendars\\r\\n\\r\\n## Usage\\r\\n\\r\\n```bash\\r\\ngws calendar +agenda\\r\\n```\\r\\n\\r\\n## Flags\\r\\n\\r\\n| Flag | Required | Default | Description |\\r\\n|------|----------|---------|-------------|\\r\\n| `--today` | — | — | Show today\'s events |\\r\\n| `--tomorrow` | — | — | Show tomorrow\'s events |\\r\\n| `--week` | — | — | Show this week\'s events |\\r\\n| `--days` | — | — | Number of days ahead to show |\\r\\n| `--calendar` | — | — | Filter to specific calendar name or ID |\\r\\n| `--timezone` | — | — | IANA timezone override (e.g. America/Denver). Defaults to Google account timezone. |\\r\\n\\r\\n## Examples\\r\\n\\r\\n```bash\\r\\ngws calendar +agenda\\r\\ngws calendar +agenda --today\\r\\ngws calendar +agenda --week --format table\\r\\ngws calendar +agenda --days 3 --calendar \'Work\'\\r\\ngws calendar +agenda --today --timezone America/New_York\\r\\n```\\r\\n\\r\\n## Tips\\r\\n\\r\\n- Read-only — never modifies events.\\r\\n- Queries all calendars by default; use --calendar to filter.\\r\\n- Uses your Google account timezone by default; override with --timezone.\\r\\n\\r\\n## See Also\\r\\n\\r\\n- [gws-shared](../gws-shared/SKILL.md) — Global flags and auth\\r\\n- [gws-calendar](../gws-calendar/SKILL.md) — All manage calendars and events commands\\r\\n### gws-calendar-insert\\r\\n---\\r\\nname: gws-calendar-insert\\r\\ndescription: \\"Google Calendar: Create a new event.\\"\\r\\nmetadata:\\r\\n  version: 0.22.1\\r\\n  openclaw:\\r\\n    category: \\"productivity\\"\\r\\n    requires:\\r\\n      bins:\\r\\n        - gws\\r\\n    cliHelp: \\"gws calendar +insert --help\\"\\r\\n---\\r\\n\\r\\n# calendar +insert\\r\\n\\r\\n> **PREREQUISITE:** Read `../gws-shared/SKILL.md` for auth, global flags, and security rules. If missing, run `gws generate-skills` to create it.\\r\\n\\r\\ncreate a new event\\r\\n\\r\\n## Usage\\r\\n\\r\\n```bash\\r\\ngws calendar +insert --summary <TEXT> --start <TIME> --end <TIME>\\r\\n```\\r\\n\\r\\n## Flags\\r\\n\\r\\n| Flag | Required | Default | Description |\\r\\n|------|----------|---------|-------------|\\r\\n| `--calendar` | — | primary | Calendar ID (default: primary) |\\r\\n| `--summary` | ✓ | — | Event summary/title |\\r\\n| `--start` | ✓ | — | Start time (ISO 8601, e.g., 2024-01-01T10:00:00Z) |\\r\\n| `--end` | ✓ | — | End time (ISO 8601) |\\r\\n| `--location` | — | — | Event location |\\r\\n| `--description` | — | — | Event description/body |\\r\\n| `--attendee` | — | — | Attendee email (can be used multiple times) |\\r\\n| `--meet` | — | — | Add a Google Meet video conference link |\\r\\n\\r\\n## Examples\\r\\n\\r\\n```bash\\r\\ngws calendar +insert --summary \'Standup\' --start \'2026-06-17T09:00:00-07:00\' --end \'2026-06-17T09:30:00-07:00\'\\r\\ngws calendar +insert --summary \'Review\' --start ... --end ... --attendee alice@example.com\\r\\ngws calendar +insert --summary \'Meet\' --start ... --end ... --meet\\r\\n```\\r\\n\\r\\n## Tips\\r\\n\\r\\n- Use RFC3339 format for times (e.g. 2026-06-17T09:00:00-07:00).\\r\\n- The --meet flag automatically adds a Google Meet link to the event.\\r\\n\\r\\n> [!CAUTION]\\r\\n> This is a **write** command — confirm with the user before executing.\\r\\n\\r\\n## See Also\\r\\n\\r\\n- [gws-shared](../gws-shared/SKILL.md) — Global flags and auth\\r\\n- [gws-calendar](../gws-calendar/SKILL.md) — All manage calendars and events commands\\r\\n### gws-chat\\r\\n---\\r\\nname: gws-chat\\r\\ndescription: \\"Google Chat: Manage Chat spaces and messages.\\"\\r\\nmetadata:\\r\\n  version: 0.22.1\\r\\n  openclaw:\\r\\n    category: \\"productivity\\"\\r\\n    requires:\\r\\n      bins:\\r\\n        - gws\\r\\n    cliHelp: \\"gws chat --help\\"\\r\\n---\\r\\n\\r\\n# chat (v1)\\r\\n\\r\\n> **PREREQUISITE:** Read `../gws-shared/SKILL.md` for auth, global flags, and security rules. If missing, run `gws generate-skills` to create it.\\r\\n\\r\\n```bash\\r\\ngws chat <resource> <method> [flags]\\r\\n```\\r\\n\\r\\n## Helper Commands\\r\\n\\r\\n| Command | Description |\\r\\n|---------|-------------|\\r\\n| [`+send`](../gws-chat-send/SKILL.md) | Send a message to a space |\\r\\n\\r\\n## API Resources\\r\\n\\r\\n### customEmojis\\r\\n\\r\\n  - `create` — Creates a custom emoji. Custom emojis are only available for Google Workspace accounts, and the administrator must turn custom emojis on for the organization. For more information, see [Learn about custom emojis in Google Chat](https://support.google.com/chat/answer/12800149) and [Manage custom emoji permissions](https://support.google.com/a/answer/12850085).\\r\\n  - `delete` — Deletes a custom emoji. By default, users can only delete custom emoji they created. [Emoji managers](https://support.google.com/a/answer/12850085) assigned by the administrator can delete any custom emoji in the organization. See [Learn about custom emojis in Google Chat](https://support.google.com/chat/answer/12800149). Custom emojis are only available for Google Workspace accounts, and the administrator must turn custom emojis on for the organization.\\r\\n  - `get` — Returns details about a custom emoji. Custom emojis are only available for Google Workspace accounts, and the administrator must turn custom emojis on for the organization. For more information, see [Learn about custom emojis in Google Chat](https://support.google.com/chat/answer/12800149) and [Manage custom emoji permissions](https://support.google.com/a/answer/12850085).\\r\\n  - `list` — Lists custom emojis visible to the authenticated user. Custom emojis are only available for Google Workspace accounts, and the administrator must turn custom emojis on for the organization. For more information, see [Learn about custom emojis in Google Chat](https://support.google.com/chat/answer/12800149) and [Manage custom emoji permissions](https://support.google.com/a/answer/12850085).\\r\\n\\r\\n### media\\r\\n\\r\\n  - `download` — Downloads media. Download is supported on the URI `/v1/media/{+name}?alt=media`.\\r\\n  - `upload` — Uploads an attachment. For an example, see [Upload media as a file attachment](https://developers.google.com/workspace/chat/upload-media-attachments).\\r\\n\\r\\n### spaces\\r\\n\\r\\n  - `completeImport` — Completes the [import process](https://developers.google.com/workspace/chat/import-data) for the specified space and makes it visible to users.\\r\\n  - `create` — Creates a space. Can be used to create a named space, or a group chat in `Import mode`. For an example, see [Create a space](https://developers.google.com/workspace/chat/create-spaces).\\r\\n  - `delete` — Deletes a named space. Always performs a cascading delete, which means that the space\'s child resources—like messages posted in the space and memberships in the space—are also deleted. For an example, see [Delete a space](https://developers.google.com/workspace/chat/delete-spaces).\\r\\n  - `findDirectMessage` — Returns the existing direct message with the specified user. If no direct message space is found, returns a `404 NOT_FOUND` error. For an example, see [Find a direct message](/chat/api/guides/v1/spaces/find-direct-message). With [app authentication](https://developers.google.com/workspace/chat/authenticate-authorize-chat-app), returns the direct message space between the specified user and the calling Chat app.\\r\\n  - `findGroupChats` — Returns all spaces with `spaceType == GROUP_CHAT`, whose human memberships contain exactly the calling user, and the users specified in `FindGroupChatsRequest.users`. Only members that have joined the conversation are supported. For an example, see [Find group chats](https://developers.google.com/workspace/chat/find-group-chats).\\r\\n  - `get` — Returns details about a space. For an example, see [Get details about a space](https://developers.google.com/workspace/chat/get-spaces).\\r\\n  - `list` — Lists spaces the caller is a member of. Group chats and DMs aren\'t listed until the first message is sent. For an example, see [List spaces](https://developers.google.com/workspace/chat/list-spaces).\\r\\n  - `patch` — Updates a space. For an example, see [Update a space](https://developers.google.com/workspace/chat/update-spaces). If you\'re updating the `displayName` field and receive the error message `ALREADY_EXISTS`, try a different display name.. An existing space within the Google Workspace organization might already use this display name.\\r\\n  - `search` — Returns a list of spaces in a Google Workspace organization based on an administrator\'s search. In the request, set `use_admin_access` to `true`. For an example, see [Search for and manage spaces](https://developers.google.com/workspace/chat/search-manage-admin).\\r\\n  - `setup` — Creates a space and adds specified users to it. The calling user is automatically added to the space, and shouldn\'t be specified as a membership in the request. For an example, see [Set up a space with initial members](https://developers.google.com/workspace/chat/set-up-spaces). To specify the human members to add, add memberships with the appropriate `membership.member.name`. To add a human user, use `users/{user}`, where `{user}` can be the email address for the user.\\r\\n  - `members` — Operations on the \'members\' resource\\r\\n  - `messages` — Operations on the \'messages\' resource\\r\\n  - `spaceEvents` — Operations on the \'spaceEvents\' resource\\r\\n\\r\\n### users\\r\\n\\r\\n  - `sections` — Operations on the \'sections\' resource\\r\\n  - `spaces` — Operations on the \'spaces\' resource\\r\\n\\r\\n## Discovering Commands\\r\\n\\r\\nBefore calling any API method, inspect it:\\r\\n\\r\\n```bash\\r\\n# Browse resources and methods\\r\\ngws chat --help\\r\\n\\r\\n# Inspect a method\'s required params, types, and defaults\\r\\ngws schema chat.<resource>.<method>\\r\\n```\\r\\n\\r\\nUse `gws schema` output to build your `--params` and `--json` flags.\\r\\n\\r\\n### gws-chat-send\\r\\n---\\r\\nname: gws-chat-send\\r\\ndescription: \\"Google Chat: Send a message to a space.\\"\\r\\nmetadata:\\r\\n  version: 0.22.1\\r\\n  openclaw:\\r\\n    category: \\"productivity\\"\\r\\n    requires:\\r\\n      bins:\\r\\n        - gws\\r\\n    cliHelp: \\"gws chat +send --help\\"\\r\\n---\\r\\n\\r\\n# chat +send\\r\\n\\r\\n> **PREREQUISITE:** Read `../gws-shared/SKILL.md` for auth, global flags, and security rules. If missing, run `gws generate-skills` to create it.\\r\\n\\r\\nSend a message to a space\\r\\n\\r\\n## Usage\\r\\n\\r\\n```bash\\r\\ngws chat +send --space <NAME> --text <TEXT>\\r\\n```\\r\\n\\r\\n## Flags\\r\\n\\r\\n| Flag | Required | Default | Description |\\r\\n|------|----------|---------|-------------|\\r\\n| `--space` | ✓ | — | Space name (e.g. spaces/AAAA...) |\\r\\n| `--text` | ✓ | — | Message text (plain text) |\\r\\n\\r\\n## Examples\\r\\n\\r\\n```bash\\r\\ngws chat +send --space spaces/AAAAxxxx --text \'Hello team!\'\\r\\n```\\r\\n\\r\\n## Tips\\r\\n\\r\\n- Use \'gws chat spaces list\' to find space names.\\r\\n- For cards or threaded replies, use the raw API instead.\\r\\n\\r\\n> [!CAUTION]\\r\\n> This is a **write** command — confirm with the user before executing.\\r\\n\\r\\n## See Also\\r\\n\\r\\n- [gws-shared](../gws-shared/SKILL.md) — Global flags and auth\\r\\n- [gws-chat](../gws-chat/SKILL.md) — All manage chat spaces and messages commands\\r\\n### gws-classroom\\r\\n---\\r\\nname: gws-classroom\\r\\ndescription: \\"Google Classroom: Manage classes, rosters, and coursework.\\"\\r\\nmetadata:\\r\\n  version: 0.22.1\\r\\n  openclaw:\\r\\n    category: \\"productivity\\"\\r\\n    requires:\\r\\n      bins:\\r\\n        - gws\\r\\n    cliHelp: \\"gws classroom --help\\"\\r\\n---\\r\\n\\r\\n# classroom (v1)\\r\\n\\r\\n> **PREREQUISITE:** Read `../gws-shared/SKILL.md` for auth, global flags, and security rules. If missing, run `gws generate-skills` to create it.\\r\\n\\r\\n```bash\\r\\ngws classroom <resource> <method> [flags]\\r\\n```\\r\\n\\r\\n## API Resources\\r\\n\\r\\n### courses\\r\\n\\r\\n  - `create` — Creates a course. The user specified in `ownerId` is the owner of the created course and added as a teacher. A non-admin requesting user can only create a course with themselves as the owner. Domain admins can create courses owned by any user within their domain. This method returns the following error codes: *…10998 tokens truncated…ingle quotes so the shell does not interpret the inner double quotes:\\r\\n  ```bash\\r\\n  gws drive files list --params \'{\\"pageSize\\": 5}\'\\r\\n  ```\\r\\n\\r\\n## Community & Feedback Etiquette\\r\\n\\r\\n- Encourage agents/users to star the repository when they find the project useful: `https://github.com/googleworkspace/cli`\\r\\n- For bugs or feature requests, direct users to open issues in the repository: `https://github.com/googleworkspace/cli/issues`\\r\\n- Before creating a new issue, **always** search existing issues and feature requests first\\r\\n- If a matching issue already exists, add context by commenting on the existing thread instead of creating a duplicate\\r\\n### gws-sheets\\r\\n---\\r\\nname: gws-sheets\\r\\ndescription: \\"Google Sheets: Read and write spreadsheets.\\"\\r\\nmetadata:\\r\\n  version: 0.22.1\\r\\n  openclaw:\\r\\n    category: \\"productivity\\"\\r\\n    requires:\\r\\n      bins:\\r\\n        - gws\\r\\n    cliHelp: \\"gws sheets --help\\"\\r\\n---\\r\\n\\r\\n# sheets (v4)\\r\\n\\r\\n> **PREREQUISITE:** Read `../gws-shared/SKILL.md` for auth, global flags, and security rules. If missing, run `gws generate-skills` to create it.\\r\\n\\r\\n```bash\\r\\ngws sheets <resource> <method> [flags]\\r\\n```\\r\\n\\r\\n## Helper Commands\\r\\n\\r\\n| Command | Description |\\r\\n|---------|-------------|\\r\\n| [`+append`](../gws-sheets-append/SKILL.md) | Append a row to a spreadsheet |\\r\\n| [`+read`](../gws-sheets-read/SKILL.md) | Read values from a spreadsheet |\\r\\n\\r\\n## API Resources\\r\\n\\r\\n### spreadsheets\\r\\n\\r\\n  - `batchUpdate` — Applies one or more updates to the spreadsheet. Each request is validated before being applied. If any request is not valid then the entire request will fail and nothing will be applied. Some requests have replies to give you some information about how they are applied. The replies will mirror the requests. For example, if you applied 4 updates and the 3rd one had a reply, then the response will have 2 empty replies, the actual reply, and another empty reply, in that order.\\r\\n  - `create` — Creates a spreadsheet, returning the newly created spreadsheet.\\r\\n  - `get` — Returns the spreadsheet at the given ID. The caller must specify the spreadsheet ID. By default, data within grids is not returned. You can include grid data in one of 2 ways: * Specify a [field mask](https://developers.google.com/workspace/sheets/api/guides/field-masks) listing your desired fields using the `fields` URL parameter in HTTP * Set the includeGridData URL parameter to true.\\r\\n  - `getByDataFilter` — Returns the spreadsheet at the given ID. The caller must specify the spreadsheet ID. For more information, see [Read, write, and search metadata](https://developers.google.com/workspace/sheets/api/guides/metadata). This method differs from GetSpreadsheet in that it allows selecting which subsets of spreadsheet data to return by specifying a dataFilters parameter. Multiple DataFilters can be specified.\\r\\n  - `developerMetadata` — Operations on the \'developerMetadata\' resource\\r\\n  - `sheets` — Operations on the \'sheets\' resource\\r\\n  - `values` — Operations on the \'values\' resource\\r\\n\\r\\n## Discovering Commands\\r\\n\\r\\nBefore calling any API method, inspect it:\\r\\n\\r\\n```bash\\r\\n# Browse resources and methods\\r\\ngws sheets --help\\r\\n\\r\\n# Inspect a method\'s required params, types, and defaults\\r\\ngws schema sheets.<resource>.<method>\\r\\n```\\r\\n\\r\\nUse `gws schema` output to build your `--params` and `--json` flags.\\r\\n\\r\\n### gws-sheets-append\\r\\n---\\r\\nname: gws-sheets-append\\r\\ndescription: \\"Google Sheets: Append a row to a spreadsheet.\\"\\r\\nmetadata:\\r\\n  version: 0.22.1\\r\\n  openclaw:\\r\\n    category: \\"productivity\\"\\r\\n    requires:\\r\\n      bins:\\r\\n        - gws\\r\\n    cliHelp: \\"gws sheets +append --help\\"\\r\\n---\\r\\n\\r\\n# sheets +append\\r\\n\\r\\n> **PREREQUISITE:** Read `../gws-shared/SKILL.md` for auth, global flags, and security rules. If missing, run `gws generate-skills` to create it.\\r\\n\\r\\nAppend a row to a spreadsheet\\r\\n\\r\\n## Usage\\r\\n\\r\\n```bash\\r\\ngws sheets +append --spreadsheet <ID>\\r\\n```\\r\\n\\r\\n## Flags\\r\\n\\r\\n| Flag | Required | Default | Description |\\r\\n|------|----------|---------|-------------|\\r\\n| `--spreadsheet` | ✓ | — | Spreadsheet ID |\\r\\n| `--values` | — | — | Comma-separated values (simple strings) |\\r\\n| `--json-values` | — | — | JSON array of rows, e.g. \'[[\\"a\\",\\"b\\"],[\\"c\\",\\"d\\"]]\' |\\r\\n\\r\\n## Examples\\r\\n\\r\\n```bash\\r\\ngws sheets +append --spreadsheet ID --values \'Alice,100,true\'\\r\\ngws sheets +append --spreadsheet ID --json-values \'[[\\"a\\",\\"b\\"],[\\"c\\",\\"d\\"]]\'\\r\\n```\\r\\n\\r\\n## Tips\\r\\n\\r\\n- Use --values for simple single-row appends.\\r\\n- Use --json-values for bulk multi-row inserts.\\r\\n\\r\\n> [!CAUTION]\\r\\n> This is a **write** command — confirm with the user before executing.\\r\\n\\r\\n## See Also\\r\\n\\r\\n- [gws-shared](../gws-shared/SKILL.md) — Global flags and auth\\r\\n- [gws-sheets](../gws-sheets/SKILL.md) — All read and write spreadsheets commands\\r\\n### gws-sheets-read\\r\\n---\\r\\nname: gws-sheets-read\\r\\ndescription: \\"Google Sheets: Read values from a spreadsheet.\\"\\r\\nmetadata:\\r\\n  version: 0.22.1\\r\\n  openclaw:\\r\\n    category: \\"productivity\\"\\r\\n    requires:\\r\\n      bins:\\r\\n        - gws\\r\\n    cliHelp: \\"gws sheets +read --help\\"\\r\\n---\\r\\n\\r\\n# sheets +read\\r\\n\\r\\n> **PREREQUISITE:** Read `../gws-shared/SKILL.md` for auth, global flags, and security rules. If missing, run `gws generate-skills` to create it.\\r\\n\\r\\nRead values from a spreadsheet\\r\\n\\r\\n## Usage\\r\\n\\r\\n```bash\\r\\ngws sheets +read --spreadsheet <ID> --range <RANGE>\\r\\n```\\r\\n\\r\\n## Flags\\r\\n\\r\\n| Flag | Required | Default | Description |\\r\\n|------|----------|---------|-------------|\\r\\n| `--spreadsheet` | ✓ | — | Spreadsheet ID |\\r\\n| `--range` | ✓ | — | Range to read (e.g. \'Sheet1!A1:B2\') |\\r\\n\\r\\n## Examples\\r\\n\\r\\n```bash\\r\\ngws sheets +read --spreadsheet ID --range \\"Sheet1!A1:D10\\"\\r\\ngws sheets +read --spreadsheet ID --range Sheet1\\r\\n```\\r\\n\\r\\n## Tips\\r\\n\\r\\n- Read-only — never modifies the spreadsheet.\\r\\n- For advanced options, use the raw values.get API.\\r\\n\\r\\n## See Also\\r\\n\\r\\n- [gws-shared](../gws-shared/SKILL.md) — Global flags and auth\\r\\n- [gws-sheets](../gws-sheets/SKILL.md) — All read and write spreadsheets commands\\r\\n### gws-slides\\r\\n---\\r\\nname: gws-slides\\r\\ndescription: \\"Google Slides: Read and write presentations.\\"\\r\\nmetadata:\\r\\n  version: 0.22.1\\r\\n  openclaw:\\r\\n    category: \\"productivity\\"\\r\\n    requires:\\r\\n      bins:\\r\\n        - gws\\r\\n    cliHelp: \\"gws slides --help\\"\\r\\n---\\r\\n\\r\\n# slides (v1)\\r\\n\\r\\n> **PREREQUISITE:** Read `../gws-shared/SKILL.md` for auth, global flags, and security rules. If missing, run `gws generate-skills` to create it.\\r\\n\\r\\n```bash\\r\\ngws slides <resource> <method> [flags]\\r\\n```\\r\\n\\r\\n## API Resources\\r\\n\\r\\n### presentations\\r\\n\\r\\n  - `batchUpdate` — Applies one or more updates to the presentation. Each request is validated before being applied. If any request is not valid, then the entire request will fail and nothing will be applied. Some requests have replies to give you some information about how they are applied. Other requests do not need to return information; these each return an empty reply. The order of replies matches that of the requests.\\r\\n  - `create` — Creates a blank presentation using the title given in the request. If a `presentationId` is provided, it is used as the ID of the new presentation. Otherwise, a new ID is generated. Other fields in the request, including any provided content, are ignored. Returns the created presentation.\\r\\n  - `get` — Gets the latest version of the specified presentation.\\r\\n  - `pages` — Operations on the \'pages\' resource\\r\\n\\r\\n## Discovering Commands\\r\\n\\r\\nBefore calling any API method, inspect it:\\r\\n\\r\\n```bash\\r\\n# Browse resources and methods\\r\\ngws slides --help\\r\\n\\r\\n# Inspect a method\'s required params, types, and defaults\\r\\ngws schema slides.<resource>.<method>\\r\\n```\\r\\n\\r\\nUse `gws schema` output to build your `--params` and `--json` flags.\\r\\n\\r\\n### gws-tasks\\r\\n---\\r\\nname: gws-tasks\\r\\ndescription: \\"Google Tasks: Manage task lists and tasks.\\"\\r\\nmetadata:\\r\\n  version: 0.22.1\\r\\n  openclaw:\\r\\n    category: \\"productivity\\"\\r\\n    requires:\\r\\n      bins:\\r\\n        - gws\\r\\n    cliHelp: \\"gws tasks --help\\"\\r\\n---\\r\\n\\r\\n# tasks (v1)\\r\\n\\r\\n> **PREREQUISITE:** Read `../gws-shared/SKILL.md` for auth, global flags, and security rules. If missing, run `gws generate-skills` to create it.\\r\\n\\r\\n```bash\\r\\ngws tasks <resource> <method> [flags]\\r\\n```\\r\\n\\r\\n## API Resources\\r\\n\\r\\n### tasklists\\r\\n\\r\\n  - `delete` — Deletes the authenticated user\'s specified task list. If the list contains assigned tasks, both the assigned tasks and the original tasks in the assignment surface (Docs, Chat Spaces) are deleted.\\r\\n  - `get` — Returns the authenticated user\'s specified task list.\\r\\n  - `insert` — Creates a new task list and adds it to the authenticated user\'s task lists. A user can have up to 2000 lists at a time.\\r\\n  - `list` — Returns all the authenticated user\'s task lists. A user can have up to 2000 lists at a time.\\r\\n  - `patch` — Updates the authenticated user\'s specified task list. This method supports patch semantics.\\r\\n  - `update` — Updates the authenticated user\'s specified task list.\\r\\n\\r\\n### tasks\\r\\n\\r\\n  - `clear` — Clears all completed tasks from the specified task list. The affected tasks will be marked as \'hidden\' and no longer be returned by default when retrieving all tasks for a task list.\\r\\n  - `delete` — Deletes the specified task from the task list. If the task is assigned, both the assigned task and the original task (in Docs, Chat Spaces) are deleted. To delete the assigned task only, navigate to the assignment surface and unassign the task from there.\\r\\n  - `get` — Returns the specified task.\\r\\n  - `insert` — Creates a new task on the specified task list. Tasks assigned from Docs or Chat Spaces cannot be inserted from Tasks Public API; they can only be created by assigning them from Docs or Chat Spaces. A user can have up to 20,000 non-hidden tasks per list and up to 100,000 tasks in total at a time.\\r\\n  - `list` — Returns all tasks in the specified task list. Doesn\'t return assigned tasks by default (from Docs, Chat Spaces). A user can have up to 20,000 non-hidden tasks per list and up to 100,000 tasks in total at a time.\\r\\n  - `move` — Moves the specified task to another position in the destination task list. If the destination list is not specified, the task is moved within its current list. This can include putting it as a child task under a new parent and/or move it to a different position among its sibling tasks. A user can have up to 2,000 subtasks per task.\\r\\n  - `patch` — Updates the specified task. This method supports patch semantics.\\r\\n  - `update` — Updates the specified task.\\r\\n\\r\\n## Discovering Commands\\r\\n\\r\\nBefore calling any API method, inspect it:\\r\\n\\r\\n```bash\\r\\n# Browse resources and methods\\r\\ngws tasks --help\\r\\n\\r\\n# Inspect a method\'s required params, types, and defaults\\r\\ngws schema tasks.<resource>.<method>\\r\\n```\\r\\n\\r\\nUse `gws schema` output to build your `--params` and `--json` flags.\\r\\n\\r\\n### gws-workflow\\r\\n---\\r\\nname: gws-workflow\\r\\ndescription: \\"Google Workflow: Cross-service productivity workflows.\\"\\r\\nmetadata:\\r\\n  version: 0.22.1\\r\\n  openclaw:\\r\\n    category: \\"productivity\\"\\r\\n    requires:\\r\\n      bins:\\r\\n        - gws\\r\\n    cliHelp: \\"gws workflow --help\\"\\r\\n---\\r\\n\\r\\n# workflow (v1)\\r\\n\\r\\n> **PREREQUISITE:** Read `../gws-shared/SKILL.md` for auth, global flags, and security rules. If missing, run `gws generate-skills` to create it.\\r\\n\\r\\n```bash\\r\\ngws workflow <resource> <method> [flags]\\r\\n```\\r\\n\\r\\n## Helper Commands\\r\\n\\r\\n| Command | Description |\\r\\n|---------|-------------|\\r\\n| [`+standup-report`](../gws-workflow-standup-report/SKILL.md) | Today\'s meetings + open tasks as a standup summary |\\r\\n| [`+meeting-prep`](../gws-workflow-meeting-prep/SKILL.md) | Prepare for your next meeting: agenda, attendees, and linked docs |\\r\\n| [`+email-to-task`](../gws-workflow-email-to-task/SKILL.md) | Convert a Gmail message into a Google Tasks entry |\\r\\n| [`+weekly-digest`](../gws-workflow-weekly-digest/SKILL.md) | Weekly summary: this week\'s meetings + unread email count |\\r\\n| [`+file-announce`](../gws-workflow-file-announce/SKILL.md) | Announce a Drive file in a Chat space |\\r\\n\\r\\n## Discovering Commands\\r\\n\\r\\nBefore calling any API method, inspect it:\\r\\n\\r\\n```bash\\r\\n# Browse resources and methods\\r\\ngws workflow --help\\r\\n\\r\\n# Inspect a method\'s required params, types, and defaults\\r\\ngws schema workflow.<resource>.<method>\\r\\n```\\r\\n\\r\\nUse `gws schema` output to build your `--params` and `--json` flags.\\r\\n\\r\\n### gws-workflow-email-to-task\\r\\n---\\r\\nname: gws-workflow-email-to-task\\r\\ndescription: \\"Google Workflow: Convert a Gmail message into a Google Tasks entry.\\"\\r\\nmetadata:\\r\\n  version: 0.22.1\\r\\n  openclaw:\\r\\n    category: \\"productivity\\"\\r\\n    requires:\\r\\n      bins:\\r\\n        - gws\\r\\n    cliHelp: \\"gws workflow +email-to-task --help\\"\\r\\n---\\r\\n\\r\\n# workflow +email-to-task\\r\\n\\r\\n> **PREREQUISITE:** Read `../gws-shared/SKILL.md` for auth, global flags, and security rules. If missing, run `gws generate-skills` to create it.\\r\\n\\r\\nConvert a Gmail message into a Google Tasks entry\\r\\n\\r\\n## Usage\\r\\n\\r\\n```bash\\r\\ngws workflow +email-to-task --message-id <ID>\\r\\n```\\r\\n\\r\\n## Flags\\r\\n\\r\\n| Flag | Required | Default | Description |\\r\\n|------|----------|---------|-------------|\\r\\n| `--message-id` | ✓ | — | Gmail message ID to convert |\\r\\n| `--tasklist` | — | @default | Task list ID (default: @default) |\\r\\n\\r\\n## Examples\\r\\n\\r\\n```bash\\r\\ngws workflow +email-to-task --message-id MSG_ID\\r\\ngws workflow +email-to-task --message-id MSG_ID --tasklist LIST_ID\\r\\n```\\r\\n\\r\\n## Tips\\r\\n\\r\\n- Reads the email subject as the task title and snippet as notes.\\r\\n- Creates a new task — confirm with the user before executing.\\r\\n\\r\\n## See Also\\r\\n\\r\\n- [gws-shared](../gws-shared/SKILL.md) — Global flags and auth\\r\\n- [gws-workflow](../gws-workflow/SKILL.md) — All cross-service productivity workflows commands\\r\\n### gws-workflow-file-announce\\r\\n---\\r\\nname: gws-workflow-file-announce\\r\\ndescription: \\"Google Workflow: Announce a Drive file in a Chat space.\\"\\r\\nmetadata:\\r\\n  version: 0.22.1\\r\\n  openclaw:\\r\\n    category: \\"productivity\\"\\r\\n    requires:\\r\\n      bins:\\r\\n        - gws\\r\\n    cliHelp: \\"gws workflow +file-announce --help\\"\\r\\n---\\r\\n\\r\\n# workflow +file-announce\\r\\n\\r\\n> **PREREQUISITE:** Read `../gws-shared/SKILL.md` for auth, global flags, and security rules. If missing, run `gws generate-skills` to create it.\\r\\n\\r\\nAnnounce a Drive file in a Chat space\\r\\n\\r\\n## Usage\\r\\n\\r\\n```bash\\r\\ngws workflow +file-announce --file-id <ID> --space <SPACE>\\r\\n```\\r\\n\\r\\n## Flags\\r\\n\\r\\n| Flag | Required | Default | Description |\\r\\n|------|----------|---------|-------------|\\r\\n| `--file-id` | ✓ | — | Drive file ID to announce |\\r\\n| `--space` | ✓ | — | Chat space name (e.g. spaces/SPACE_ID) |\\r\\n| `--message` | — | — | Custom announcement message |\\r\\n| `--format` | — | — | Output format: json (default), table, yaml, csv |\\r\\n\\r\\n## Examples\\r\\n\\r\\n```bash\\r\\ngws workflow +file-announce --file-id FILE_ID --space spaces/ABC123\\r\\ngws workflow +file-announce --file-id FILE_ID --space spaces/ABC123 --message \'Check this out!\'\\r\\n```\\r\\n\\r\\n## Tips\\r\\n\\r\\n- This is a write command — sends a Chat message.\\r\\n- Use `gws drive +upload` first to upload the file, then announce it here.\\r\\n- Fetches the file name from Drive to build the announcement.\\r\\n\\r\\n## See Also\\r\\n\\r\\n- [gws-shared](../gws-shared/SKILL.md) — Global flags and auth\\r\\n- [gws-workflow](../gws-workflow/SKILL.md) — All cross-service productivity workflows commands\\r\\n### gws-workflow-meeting-prep\\r\\n---\\r\\nname: gws-workflow-meeting-prep\\r\\ndescription: \\"Google Workflow: Prepare for your next meeting: agenda, attendees, and linked docs.\\"\\r\\nmetadata:\\r\\n  version: 0.22.1\\r\\n  openclaw:\\r\\n    category: \\"productivity\\"\\r\\n    requires:\\r\\n      bins:\\r\\n        - gws\\r\\n    cliHelp: \\"gws workflow +meeting-prep --help\\"\\r\\n---\\r\\n\\r\\n# workflow +meeting-prep\\r\\n\\r\\n> **PREREQUISITE:** Read `../gws-shared/SKILL.md` for auth, global flags, and security rules. If missing, run `gws generate-skills` to create it.\\r\\n\\r\\nToday\'s meetings + open tasks as a standup summary\\r\\n\\r\\n## Usage\\r\\n\\r\\n```bash\\r\\ngws workflow +standup-report\\r\\n```\\r\\n\\r\\n## Flags\\r\\n\\r\\n| Flag | Required | Default | Description |\\r\\n|------|----------|---------|-------------|\\r\\n| `--format` | — | — | Output format: json (default), table, yaml, csv |\\r\\n\\r\\n## Examples\\r\\n\\r\\n```bash\\r\\ngws workflow +standup-report\\r\\ngws workflow +standup-report --format table\\r\\n```\\r\\n\\r\\n## Tips\\r\\n\\r\\n- Read-only — never modifies data.\\r\\n- Combines calendar agenda (today) with tasks list.\\r\\n\\r\\n## See Also\\r\\n\\r\\n- [gws-shared](../gws-shared/SKILL.md) — Global flags and auth\\r\\n- [gws-workflow](../gws-workflow/SKILL.md) — All cross-service productivity workflows commands\\r\\n### gws-workflow-weekly-digest\\r\\n---\\r\\nname: gws-workflow-weekly-digest\\r\\ndescription: \\"Google Workflow: Weekly summary: this week\'s meetings + unread email count.\\"\\r\\nmetadata:\\r\\n  version: 0.22.1\\r\\n  openclaw:\\r\\n    category: \\"productivity\\"\\r\\n    requires:\\r\\n      bins:\\r\\n        - gws\\r\\n    cliHelp: \\"gws workflow +weekly-digest --help\\"\\r\\n---\\r\\n\\r\\n# workflow +weekly-digest\\r\\n\\r\\n> **PREREQUISITE:** Read `../gws-shared/SKILL.md` for auth, global flags, and security rules. [{'type': 'input_text', 'text': 'Script completed\nWall time 12.3 seconds\nOutput:\n'}, {'type': 'input_text', 'text': '{"chunk_id":"1f56bb","wall_time_seconds":1.4988022,"exit_code":0,"original_token_count":4889,"output":"### chief-of-staff\\r\\n---\\r\\nname: chief-of-staff\\r\\ndescription: Pursue a long-running goal in a single session by co-ordinating subagents.\\r\\ndisable-model-invocation: true\\r\\n---\\r\\n\\r\\nYou are a chief of staff, co-ordinating subagents and schedules to pursue a long-running goal. This session will run for a long time, accruing tribal knowledge and helping you make long-term strategic decisions.\\r\\n\\r\\nYou are the Directly Responsible Individual for this goal. You are empowered to think much longer-term than you\'re used to. You must think on two tracks simultaneously:\\r\\n\\r\\n- Tactical: how do I complete the immediate task?\\r\\n- Strategic: how do I modify the environment to improve the outcomes of the _next_ task?\\r\\n\\r\\n## Schedules\\r\\n\\r\\nHarness-permitting, you will suggest recurring schedules which can help in achieving the goal.\\r\\n\\r\\n## Subagents\\r\\n\\r\\nAll work should be done in subagents. Protect your context window.\\r\\n\\r\\nUse background agents so you can stay in active dialogue with the user.\\r\\n\\r\\nCommunication to and from subagents should be sparse. Communicate primarily through **context pointers**: research notes, previous commits, and others. Don\'t duplicate information already available via pointers.\\r\\n\\r\\n## Strategic View\\r\\n\\r\\nAs part of any and all work, FIRST consider how the environment the agents operate in might be improved. Agents thrive in the **pit of success**:\\r\\n\\r\\n- API\'s and functions which are extremely constrained and limited\\r\\n- Lint rules which force correctness\\r\\n- CODING_STANDARDS.md files which let code reviewers enforce best practices\\r\\n\\r\\nThey also need relevant **data sources** to succeed:\\r\\n\\r\\n- Logs from critical running processes, like dev servers (or production logs)\\r\\n- Access to test environment databases\\r\\n- Access to the browser (when necessary) for clicking around and taking screenshots\\r\\n\\r\\nFinally, create environments (and codebases) that obey the **\\"no workarounds\\"** rule:\\r\\n\\r\\n- No one-off workarounds, or hacks that bypass established processes\\r\\n- Any deviations from conventions must be fixed proactively, before feature work is done\\r\\n\\r\\nBe relentless in improving the environment. Use every user message as an excuse to search for these improvements.\\r\\n### claude-handoff\\r\\n---\\r\\nname: claude-handoff\\r\\ndescription: Hand the current conversation off to a fresh background agent that picks up the work immediately.\\r\\nargument-hint: \\"What will the next session be used for?\\"\\r\\ndisable-model-invocation: true\\r\\n---\\r\\n\\r\\nWrite a handoff summary of the current conversation so a fresh agent can continue the work. Save it to the temporary directory of the user\'s OS, then launch a background agent seeded with it as its prompt: `claude --bg --name \\"<descriptive name>\\" -- \\"$(cat <summary file>)\\"`. Passing the file keeps the shell from running backticks or expanding `$` in the summary. It starts in the current working directory and returns immediately; the user manages it with `claude agents`.\\r\\n\\r\\nAlways pass `-n`/`--name` with a descriptive name (e.g. `--name \\"Fix login bug\\"`); it sets the display name shown in the job list, session picker, and terminal title.\\r\\n\\r\\nInclude a \\"suggested skills\\" section in the summary, naming which skills the next agent should call the Skill tool for.\\r\\n\\r\\nDo not duplicate content already captured in other artifacts (specs, plans, ADRs, issues, commits, diffs). Reference them by path or URL instead.\\r\\n\\r\\nRedact any sensitive information, such as API keys, passwords, or personally identifiable information, since the summary becomes the agent\'s prompt.\\r\\n\\r\\nIf the user passed arguments, treat them as a description of what the next session will focus on and tailor the summary accordingly.\\r\\n### consultation-followup-drafts\\r\\n---\\r\\nname: consultation-followup-drafts\\r\\ndescription: \\"Daily: detect past consultations with Gemini notes and draft (not send) personalized follow-up emails from the transcript\\"\\r\\n---\\r\\n\\r\\nYou are Joshua\'s email drafting partner for aspiringattorneys.com (LSAT tutoring). Each run, find consultations that just happened and draft a personalized follow-up email from the meeting transcript, for Joshua to review. NEVER send. Only create Gmail drafts.\\r\\n\\r\\nSTEP 1 — Read voice + template (required):\\r\\n- Read C:/Users/Joshu/dev/ai-os/wiki/CONSULTATION-FOLLOW-UP-TEMPLATE.md (the real template, rebuilt 2026-09-11 from sent mail; the old PDF and archive paths are retired)\\r\\n- Read C:/Users/Joshu/dev/ai-os/wiki/teaching-voice.md\\r\\nUse the template body verbatim. The only variables are the first name, the 7Sage line (in or out), an optional delay apology, and one sentence confirming an agreed weekly slot. Do NOT write a personalized recap sentence. No em dashes.\\r\\n\\r\\nSTEP 2 — Find consultations ready for follow-up. Use `gws calendar events list` (or the Gemini notes already saved under students/_other-sessions/) to list events whose title contains \\"Consultation\\" from the last 4 days that are already in the past (ended before now). For each, look for a \\"Notes by Gemini\\" attachment or a linked Transcript Google Doc on the event. If there is no such attachment yet, SKIP it (the call may not have happened or notes aren\'t ready).\\r\\n\\r\\nSTEP 3 — Read the transcript. For each event that has Gemini notes, use `gws drive files get`/export on the attached doc, or read the saved copy in students/_other-sessions/. Extract: the student\'s name and email (from the event attendees), the details to mirror (diagnostic/current score, target score, study platform, exam timeline, main struggles), and the \\"Next steps\\" action items.\\r\\n\\r\\nSTEP 4 — Check it isn\'t already handled. Use `gws gmail users messages list --params \'{\\"userId\\":\\"me\\",\\"q\\":\\"<email>\\"}\'` to find any existing thread with that attendee. If a next-steps / follow-up email has already been sent to them since the consultation date, SKIP (one follow-up per consultation). If they already booked and paid, draft the short onboarding note from the template instead of the sales-y next-steps email.\\r\\n\\r\\nSTEP 5 — Draft using wiki/CONSULTATION-FOLLOW-UP-TEMPLATE.md. Default rate tier $45/$40/$35. Include the 7Sage line only if the notes say they use 7Sage. Greeting \\"Hi [First name],\\". Sign \\"Best,\\r\\n\\r\\nJoshua\\". Create it with `gws gmail users drafts create` (raw RFC822, base64url), replying in the existing thread (threadId + In-Reply-To) if one exists, otherwise a new draft with subject \\"Next steps + tutoring options\\". Do NOT send.\\r\\n\\r\\nSTEP 6 — Report: for each consultation, the student\'s name/email, the detail you mirrored, which variant you used, and that a draft is waiting in Gmail for review. If no consultations were ready, say so in one line. Flag anything uncertain (e.g. couldn\'t tell if they already booked) so Joshua can check before sending.\\r\\n### consultation-inquiry-drafts\\r\\n---\\r\\nname: consultation-inquiry-drafts\\r\\ndescription: \\"Daily sweep: draft, but do not send, personalized consultation-link replies to new LSAT tutoring inquiries\\"\\r\\n---\\r\\n\\r\\n# Consultation Inquiry Drafts\\r\\n\\r\\nFind new LSAT tutoring inquiries and prepare Gmail drafts for Joshua to review. Never send. AI-generated replies remain drafts unless Joshua separately approves the exact message.\\r\\n\\r\\n## Required context\\r\\n\\r\\nBefore drafting:\\r\\n\\r\\n1. Read `C:/Users/Joshu/dev/ai-os/wiki/teaching-voice.md`.\\r\\n2. Read `C:/Users/Joshu/dev/ai-os/context/work.md` for current offers, booking, and billing rules.\\r\\n3. Use Gmail only through the `gws` CLI. Do not use Google connector MCPs.\\r\\n4. If the sender may already be a student, check `students/<name>/` first. Use Gmail and other live systems only when the student file does not resolve identity or current state.\\r\\n\\r\\n## Find eligible inquiries\\r\\n\\r\\nSearch Gmail for recent inbox threads that appear to be genuine new tutoring inquiries. A useful starting query is:\\r\\n\\r\\n```text\\r\\nin:inbox newer_than:2d -in:sent\\r\\n```\\r\\n\\r\\nInclude people asking about tutoring, rates, availability, consultations, referrals, or how to begin.\\r\\n\\r\\nSkip:\\r\\n\\r\\n- Existing-student logistics.\\r\\n- Booking and calendar notifications.\\r\\n- Newsletters and spam.\\r\\n- Any thread Joshua has already answered.\\r\\n- Anyone who has already paid or moved past consultation. Route those cases according to their actual student and payment state.\\r\\n\\r\\nUnread status is a clue, not proof that a reply is owed. Inspect the thread and confirm Joshua has not already responded.\\r\\n\\r\\n## Drafting rules\\r\\n\\r\\nEach reply must:\\r\\n\\r\\n- React to at least one real detail from the inquiry, such as a score, test date, platform, referral, plateau, or specific struggle.\\r\\n- Use a brief general acknowledgment only when the inquiry contains no useful detail.\\r\\n- Invite the prospect to a free consultation using `https://cal.com/joshua-jtx5ud/consultation`.\\r\\n- Explain the consultation in one short, low-pressure sentence.\\r\\n- Mention the current rate, `$40/h`, only when the person asks about price, rates, cost, or affordability.\\r\\n- Use a brief apology near the opening when Joshua\'s reply is more than about 24 hours late.\\r\\n- Stay under roughly 120 words, unless the inquiry genuinely requires more.\\r\\n- Use prose only, no bullets and no em dashes.\\r\\n- Default to `Hi [First name],` and `Best,\\\\nJoshua`. Use `Hey` only when the sender\'s tone and relationship clearly support it.\\r\\n- Invite the person to reply if the booking link does not work.\\r\\n\\r\\nDo not copy canned situation lines blindly. Mirror the person\'s message in natural language and follow the current teaching-voice page.\\r\\n\\r\\n## Gmail draft behavior\\r\\n\\r\\nCreate the draft through `gws`. Reply inside the existing Gmail thread whenever one exists. Preserve the thread context and reply headers rather than starting a new conversation. Do not send.\\r\\n\\r\\n## Report and log\\r\\n\\r\\nReport each prospect\'s name, email, the detail mirrored, and that a Gmail draft is waiting for review. Flag uncertain identity, prior-contact, pricing, or student-status cases.\\r\\n\\r\\nAppend each created draft to `wiki/send-ledger.md` with status `drafted`. Gmail remains the authority for whether anything was actually sent.\\r\\n### guided-drill-assignment\\r\\n---\\r\\nname: guided-drill-assignment\\r\\ndescription: Use this whenever Joshua asks to look at a student\'s transcript, choose an appropriate LSAT U guided drill, verify the drill works, assign it through the platform, or confirm that the student received a clear notification. This skill covers the full workflow from transcript review to guided drill recommendation, platform/browser QA, assignment, and notification verification.\\r\\n---\\r\\n\\r\\n# Guided Drill Assignment\\r\\n\\r\\nUse this skill to turn student performance context into a verified guided drill assignment in LSAT U.\\r\\n\\r\\nThe operating standard is: do not merely recommend a drill. Choose the right drill from the student\'s recent transcript/context, verify the drill actually launches and is wired correctly, assign it through the platform, then verify the student\'s notification surface.\\r\\n\\r\\n## Inputs\\r\\n\\r\\nExpect one or more of:\\r\\n\\r\\n- A student name or shorthand, such as `C`, `C. Alexander`, or another current student.\\r\\n- A request to inspect a recent transcript, chat export, meeting note, student page, or platform record.\\r\\n- A request to find an appropriate guided drill.\\r\\n- A request to assign a drill and make sure the student is notified.\\r\\n\\r\\nIf the student identity is ambiguous and cannot be safely inferred from local context, ask one concise clarifying question before assigning anything.\\r\\n\\r\\n## Required Context\\r\\n\\r\\nFor LSAT U vault work, follow the vault operating order before making a recommendation:\\r\\n\\r\\n1. Read `wiki/hot.md`.\\r\\n2. Read `../ai-os-projects/lsatu/README.md`.\\r\\n3. Read `wiki/dashboard.md`.\\r\\n4. Read the relevant student page under `students/`.\\r\\n5. Read the student\'s `assignment-log.md` if it exists so you do not repeat assigned work unless Joshua explicitly asks for a repeat.\\r\\n6. Read `wiki/guided-drill-verification-log.md` so already-verified drills are not re-QA\'d unnecessarily.\\r\\n7. Search all available transcripts, transcript downloads, chat exports, and meeting notes for that student.\\r\\n8. Sort candidate transcript/context files by the actual meeting date, not file modification time, and use the most up-to-date transcript as the primary source of truth.\\r\\n\\r\\nPrefer local sources first. Do not invent student weaknesses or assignment history. If an older transcript conflicts with a newer one, follow the newer transcript and mention the older file only as background.\\r\\n\\r\\nUseful searches:\\r\\n\\r\\n```bash\\r\\nrg -n \\"student-name-or-shorthand|student full name|student email\\" wiki raw students projects\\r\\nfind students -path \\"*transcript*\\" -type f | rg -i \\"student-slug|student-name\\"\\r\\n```\\r\\n\\r\\n## Drill Selection\\r\\n\\r\\nChoose the drill by matching the student\'s most recent need to the drill\'s pedagogical purpose.\\r\\n\\r\\nEvaluate:\\r\\n\\r\\n- Newest transcript evidence by meeting date: missed concepts, confusion, pacing, task avoidance, question type weakness, or reasoning pattern weakness.\\r\\n- Student readiness: assign teach-first drills when the student needs instruction, not a cold test.\\r\\n- Drill metadata: title, slug, week/module, question type, tags, pool size, question count, estimated time.\\r\\n- Platform constraints: student must have classroom and drill access.\\r\\n- Assignment history: avoid assigning a drill already present in the student\'s `assignment-log.md` unless Joshua explicitly wants a repeat or the log says it should be repeated.\\r\\n\\r\\nWhen the best drill is not obvious, produce a short ranked recommendation before assigning:\\r\\n\\r\\n```markdown\\r\\nRecommended: <drill title>\\r\\nReason: <one sentence tied to transcript evidence>\\r\\nBackup: <second drill title, only if meaningfully close>\\r\\nDo not assign yet because: <only include if blocked>\\r\\n```\\r\\n\\r\\nIf the user has already asked to assign and the best choice is clear, proceed without stopping.\\r\\n\\r\\n## Repo Checks\\r\\n\\r\\nBefore using a drill, verify that it exists in the app data and is wired to the platform.\\r\\n\\r\\nCommon files to inspect:\\r\\n\\r\\n- `data/guided-drills/_seed.json`\\r\\n- `src/data/guidedDrillHtmlManifest.ts`\\r\\n- `src/lib/guidedDrills.ts`\\r\\n- `src/pages/Drill.tsx`\\r\\n- `src/pages/teacher/desk/library/DeskLibraryGuidedDrillsSurface.tsx`\\r\\n- `src/lib/classroomNotify.ts`\\r\\n- `src/lib/assignmentEmail.ts`\\r\\n\\r\\nConfirm:\\r\\n\\r\\n- The drill slug and title exist.\\r\\n- The drill has enough eligible questions for the configured count.\\r\\n- The guided assignment flow creates `guided_drill_assignments`.\\r\\n- The classroom item is created from the assignment source row.\\r\\n- Completion writes `completed_at` and `status: completed`.\\r\\n- Notification code attempts inbox, bell, and email where applicable.\\r\\n\\r\\nRun targeted tests if the repo is available:\\r\\n\\r\\n```bash\\r\\nnpm test -- --run src/lib/guidedDrillNavigation.test.ts src/lib/classroomItems.test.ts src/components/mainhub/TodayFocusPanel.test.ts\\r\\n```\\r\\n\\r\\nIf tests cannot be run, say why and continue with browser verification.\\r\\n\\r\\n## Browser Verification\\r\\n\\r\\nUse the in-app browser when available. The usual admin surface is:\\r\\n\\r\\n```text\\r\\nhttps://lsatprep.study/teacher?ws=library&tab=guided-drills\\r\\n```\\r\\n\\r\\nBefore doing full launch QA, check `wiki/guided-drill-verification-log.md`.\\r\\n\\r\\nIf the selected drill is already listed as `verified-working`:\\r\\n\\r\\n1. Do not repeat full preview/start-runner verification.\\r\\n2. Cite the existing verification log entry.\\r\\n3. Continue with student profile/access checks and assignment flow.\\r\\n\\r\\nIf the selected drill is not yet verified, run this sequence:\\r\\n\\r\\nVerification sequence:\\r\\n\\r\\n1. Open the teacher guided drills library.\\r\\n2. Search the exact drill title or slug.\\r\\n3. Confirm the visible card shows the expected title, module/week, question count, and tags.\\r\\n4. Open the preview.\\r\\n5. Confirm the launch card renders with the expected title, estimated time, and question count.\\r\\n6. Click `Start Drill`.\\r\\n7. Confirm the real drill runner loads with question text, answer choices, controls, and the expected URL parameters or question ids.\\r\\n8. Return to the guided drill library before assigning.\\r\\n\\r\\nDo not call the drill \\"perfect\\" unless the above checks passed. Prefer \\"verified to launch and load the runner\\" over broader claims.\\r\\n\\r\\nExisting noisy console warnings that do not block launch should be reported only if relevant.\\r\\n\\r\\nAfter a new drill passes browser verification, add it to `wiki/guided-drill-verification-log.md` with date, slug, evidence, and `verified-working` status.\\r\\n\\r\\n## Assignment Flow\\r\\n\\r\\nAssign through the platform, not by manually inserting rows, unless the user explicitly asks for a backend-only repair.\\r\\n\\r\\nTeacher UI sequence:\\r\\n\\r\\n1. On the exact drill card, click `Assign`.\\r\\n2. In the assign dialog, search/select the intended student only.\\r\\n3. Scope checks to the dialog so sidebar or to-do rail text does not create false positives.\\r\\n4. Confirm the dialog says exactly one selected student, unless the user requested multiple students.\\r\\n5. Click the primary button, usually `Assign to 1 student`.\\r\\n6. Wait for the success toast.\\r\\n\\r\\nIf there is any sign that the wrong student is selected, stop before clicking assign.\\r\\n\\r\\n## Post-Assignment Verification\\r\\n\\r\\nAfter assignment, verify live state rather than relying only on the toast.\\r\\n\\r\\nVerify:\\r\\n\\r\\n- Student identity and access flags.\\r\\n- Guided drill assignment row.\\r\\n- Classroom item row visible to the student.\\r\\n- Unread bell notification row.\\r\\n- Notification link points to the assignment route or classroom route.\\r\\n- Email leg, if available through logs or returned notification result.\\r\\n\\r\\nAfter verification, update the student\'s `assignment-log.md` with the drill, slug, reason, platform evidence, notification evidence, and current status. If the file does not exist, create it.\\r\\n\\r\\nExpected tables/objects:\\r\\n\\r\\n- `profiles`\\r\\n- `guided_drills`\\r\\n- `guided_drill_assignments`\\r\\n- `classroom_items`\\r\\n- `notifications`\\r\\n- `email_send_log`, if accessible\\r\\n\\r\\nProtect secrets:\\r\\n\\r\\n- Do not print auth tokens.\\r\\n- Do not print service-role keys.\\r\\n- Do not expose full student email addresses unless the user explicitly needs them.\\r\\n- Redact email recipients in final reports.\\r\\n\\r\\nExample final verification fields:\\r\\n\\r\\n```markdown\\r\\nAssignment:\\r\\n- student: <display name>\\r\\n- drill: <title>\\r\\n- assignment status: assigned\\r\\n- classroom item: visible_to_student true\\r\\n- bell notification: unread assignment notification exists\\r\\n- email: verified via log / returned OK by platform / not independently verified\\r\\n```\\r\\n\\r\\n## Final Response\\r\\n\\r\\nKeep the final response short and operational.\\r\\n\\r\\nUse this shape:\\r\\n\\r\\n```markdown\\r\\nAssigned <drill title> to <student>.\\r\\n\\r\\nVerified:\\r\\n- <drill launch/browser check>\\r\\n- <assignment row/classroom visibility>\\r\\n- <notification evidence>\\r\\n- <tests, if run>\\r\\n\\r\\nEmail: <verified status or limitation>\\r\\n```\\r\\n\\r\\nIf assignment was not completed, say exactly where it stopped and what is needed next.\\r\\n\\r\\nAvoid overstating. \\"Clear in-app notification exists\\" is acceptable only after verifying a notification row or student-facing UI evidence.\\r\\n\\r\\n## Example From Prior Workflow\\r\\n\\r\\nStudent: C. Alexander.\\r\\n\\r\\nSelected drill: `Necessary Assumption - First Taste`, slug `w2-07-necessary-assumption-first-taste`.\\r\\n\\r\\nReasoning: transcript context indicated Necessary Assumption needed a teach-first, calibrated drill. The drill is W2.7, 10 questions, 60 minutes, with Necessary Assumption plus Comparison/Causation tags.\\r\\n\\r\\nVerification performed:\\r\\n\\r\\n- Opened guided drill library.\\r\\n- Found the exact card.\\r\\n- Opened preview.\\r\\n- Started the drill.\\r\\n- Confirmed the runner loaded with 10 question ids and real question content.\\r\\n- Assigned to only C. Alexander through the dialog.\\r\\n- Verified the assignment row, classroom item, and unread bell notification.\\r\\n\\r\\nUse this as a pattern, not as a default assignment for every student.\\r\\n"}'}]
