[{'type': 'input_text', 'text': 'Script completed\nWall time 7.7 seconds\nOutput:\n'}, {'type': 'input_text', 'text': '{"chunk_id":"902fe4","wall_time_seconds":1.1996339,"exit_code":0,"original_token_count":7813,"output":"Warning: truncated output (original token count: 7813)\\nTotal output lines: 543\\n\\n### ingest\\r\\n---\\r\\nname: ingest\\r\\ndescription: >\\r\\n  The single front door for adding sources to the current knowledge base. Use\\r\\n  for \\"ingest this\\", \\"process this source\\", \\"file these notes\\", \\"add this to\\r\\n  my second brain\\", \\"ingest the latest clips\\", or a supplied document meant\\r\\n  to become saved knowledge. Finds the input, checks content hashes, preserves\\r\\n  provenance, and compiles it into linked wiki pages. Session write-ups and\\r\\n  student-facing post-session recaps belong to post-session-recap.\\r\\nallowed-tools: Bash Read Write Edit Glob Grep\\r\\n---\\r\\n\\r\\n# Ingest sources into the current brain\\r\\n\\r\\nOne public skill owns discovery, duplicate checks, preservation, routing, and\\r\\nwiki compilation. `second-brain-ingest` is a compatibility name for this same\\r\\nworkflow, not another pipeline. Read the internal\\r\\n`references/wiki-compilation.md` when processing knowledge sources.\\r\\n\\r\\n## Resolve the vault and schema first\\r\\n\\r\\nFind the vault root from the current workspace and its nearest instruction files.\\r\\nRead `system/schema/llm-wiki.md` relative to that root. It is the authority for\\r\\nfolder conventions, page metadata, provenance, index, log, and ingest/query/lint\\r\\nworkflows. Do not assume a saved Windows or Mac path. If no schema exists in the\\r\\ntarget vault, report that gap before changing its structure; never initialize a\\r\\nsecond vault to solve a request about an existing one.\\r\\n\\r\\n## Route first\\r\\n\\r\\nIdentify what is being ingested, then jump to that section. If it is genuinely\\r\\nambiguous, ask once. Do not guess and file it somewhere wrong.\\r\\n\\r\\n| Input | Where it lands | Section |\\r\\n|---|---|---|\\r\\n| Web clip from Obsidian Web Clipper (`.md` in `raw/inbox/`) | `raw/inbox/` | [Clips](#clips) |\\r\\n| A clip that is a YouTube / video page | `raw/inbox/` | [Clips](#clips), read via `watch` |\\r\\n| Gemini \\"Notes by Gemini\\" from a live session (this week, last week) | Google Drive | [Transcripts, live](#transcripts-live) |\\r\\n| Archival Gemini `.docx` / `.txt` (Apr to Jul 2026 Takeout batch) | `raw/data-about-me/transcripts/` | [Transcripts, archival](#transcripts-archival) |\\r\\n| Superwhisper `recordings/` dirs (`meta.json` + `output.wav`) or `settings.json` | wherever they were dropped | hand to `superwhisper`; not this skill\'s |\\r\\n| Student evidence: PT score report, screenshot, homework export | `~/Downloads`, chat attachment | [Student evidence](#student-evidence) |\\r\\n| A source document meant to become wiki knowledge | `raw/` | dedupe below, then read `references/wiki-compilation.md` |\\r\\n| Takeout or platform dump | `raw/data-about-me/` | [Bulk exports](#bulk-exports) |\\r\\n\\r\\nKnowledge-source compilation is this skill\'s internal reference. `post-session-recap`\\r\\nowns the complete student-facing session write-up workflow. A request only to\\r\\nretrieve or file a transcript stays narrow; a recap request goes directly to that\\r\\nskill without asking for a second activation.\\r\\n\\r\\n## Always, before any pipeline\\r\\n\\r\\n1. **Find the file without asking where it is.** Search newest-first:\\r\\n   ```\\r\\n   raw/inbox/   raw/sources/   ~/Downloads/   ~/Desktop/   students/*/transcript-downloads/\\r\\n   ```\\r\\n   Ask only if that comes up empty. He has answered \\"where is it\\" too many\\r\\n   times. `raw/inbox/` is the single intake queue; the old top-level\\r\\n   `Clippings/` folder was folded into `raw/sources/clips/` on 2026-09-08, so a\\r\\n   `Clippings/` path in an old note is stale.\\r\\n2. **Dedupe by SHA-256, not by name.** On Windows use `Get-FileHash` or\\r\\n   Python `hashlib`. Check existing archive manifests, source-page metadata,\\r\\n   and dated ingest entries. A matching filename alone is not proof. A matching\\r\\n   hash with completed wiki output means report the existing output and stop.\\r\\n   An archived hash without finished output means resume compilation, not\\r\\n   discard the source. Never delete duplicates.\\r\\n3. **Check the log and source summary.** Record whether the candidate was\\r\\n   previously processed and whether this is a new revision. Preserve both\\r\\n   generations when content changed. A deliberate re-ingest updates the\\r\\n   existing source page with revision provenance, not a duplicate truth.\\r\\n4. **Preserve the input byte-for-byte.** Copy external attachments or inbox\\r\\n   inputs to an appropriate `raw/sources/` archive and verify the SHA-256 before\\r\\n   citing the preserved copy. Record origin, URL/author/date when known,\\r\\n   capture date, archived date, filename, size, and hash. Do not move, delete,\\r\\n   overwrite, or edit original source bytes. Do not follow symlinks outside a\\r\\n   registered source root. Existing archived inputs can be read in place.\\r\\n\\r\\n## Clips\\r\\n\\r\\nObsidian Web Clipper writes `.md` files to `raw/inbox/`. Anything else sitting\\r\\nthere (a `recordings/` tree, a `settings.json`) is not a clip; route it by the\\r\\ntable above and tell Joshua it was in the wrong place rather than processing it\\r\\nhere.\\r\\n\\r\\n1. List `raw/inbox/*.md` newest-first. \\"The latest\\" means the newest; a named\\r\\n   topic means match on it; several new ones means list them and ask which.\\r\\n2. Dedupe (above).\\r\\n3. Read the clip fully. If it is a video page with no transcript, use the\\r\\n   appropriate transcript intake workflow; do not treat its thumbnail as evidence.\\r\\n4. Copy and hash-verify the clip into `raw/sources/clips/<slug>/`, using\\r\\n   `PROVENANCE.md` and `SHA256SUMS`. Reuse an existing identical archive.\\r\\n   Preserve the inbox original. Processed status comes from its hash, source\\r\\n   page, and log, not from whether the original still exists in the inbox.\\r\\n5. Follow `references/wiki-compilation.md` through the source summary,\\r\\n   relevant existing pages, index update, log entry, and verification.\\r\\n\\r\\nOne source at a time unless Joshua explicitly asks for batch work. Discuss\\r\\nimportant takeaways as part of the work. An explicit instruction to implement,\\r\\nfile, or ingest with a stated focus authorizes completing that scope; do not\\r\\nintroduce an extra confirmation step. Ask when unresolved emphasis, identity,\\r\\nor contradictory evidence materially changes what should be written.\\r\\n\\r\\n## Transcripts, live\\r\\n\\r\\nGemini writes \\"Notes by Gemini\\" docs to Google Drive after each Meet session.\\r\\nThe brain\'s copy is `students/<slug>/transcript-downloads/YYYY-MM-DD-<slug>-notes-by-gemini.md`\\r\\n(primary record: the brain is its only home). Getting them there is step 1 of\\r\\n`post-session-recap/references/transcript-intake-and-record.md`; follow that section exactly (Calendar sweep by guest email,\\r\\nDrive sweep for unattached docs, export as `text/plain`, resolve the person\\r\\nwith `students/_aliases.md`, consultations and unknowns to\\r\\n`students/_other-sessions/`). It is the single source of truth for the pull;\\r\\ndo not re-derive the `gws` commands here.\\r\\n\\r\\nThen, per transcript that is new on disk:\\r\\n\\r\\n1. Read the whole transcript, not the Gemini summary at the top. The summary\\r\\n   flattens what the student actually did; the distillation has to name the\\r\\n   answer they picked and the line they misread.\\r\\n2. Append to the student\'s `teaching-notes.md` (create it from a sibling if the\\r\\n   folder lacks one; it is a standard primary file): what was taught, where they\\r\\n   struggled, what was assigned, what to follow up. Dated heading, append-only,\\r\\n   never regenerate.\\r\\n3. Anything needing an action goes to `open-loops.md` (same rules).\\r\\n4. Add one line to `transcripts.md` so the folder\'s inventory matches disk.\\r\\n5. Never write to a `*.generated.md` file; those mirror a live backend.\\r\\n6. Append to `wiki/log.md`.\\r\\n\\r\\nDone means every session in the window either has its transcript on disk and\\r\\ndistilled, or is listed in the log as \\"no Gemini doc anywhere\\" with the date and\\r\\nstudent, so the next session does not sweep it again.\\r\\n\\r\\nIf Joshua requests a session write-up or recap, activate `post-session-recap`\\r\\nand complete its workflow; do not stop at telling him another skill is needed.\\r\\n\\r\\n## Transcripts, archival\\r\\n\\r\\nThe Takeout batch of 52 `.docx` / `.txt` files in `raw/data-about-me/transcripts/`\\r\\n(2026-04-28 to 2026-07-15) was distilled on 2026-07-20 (`wiki/log.md`). It is\\r\\ngit-ignored PII; never read the folder wholesale into context.\\r\\n\\r\\n**Start with the inventory. Do not re-derive the mapping by hand.**\\r\\n\\r\\n```\\r\\npython system/scripts/transcript-inventory.py              # full report\\r\\npython system/scripts/transcript-inventory.py --unmatched  # only the gaps\\r\\npython system/scripts/transcript-inventory.py --json       # machine-readable\\r\\npython system/scripts/transcript-inventory.py --text \\"<file>.docx\\"   # one transcript as text\\r\\n```\\r\\n\\r\\nIt maps each file to a folder using `students/_aliases.md`, knows that former\\r\\nstudents live in `students/non-students/`, and prints what it cannot resolve.\\r\\n`--text` exists because this box has no python-docx and no pandoc; it is how a\\r\\n`.docx` gets read. The script is read-only.\\r\\n\\r\\nFor an unmapped file, resolve before filing:\\r\\n- a name variant of an existing student: add it under `## Aliases` in\\r\\n  `students/_aliases.md`, re-run, continue;\\r\\n- a consultation or one-off: add under `## Prospects, no record yet` (the\\r\\n  section the script parses) so it stops surfacing;\\r\\n- a real recurring student with no folder: **ask Joshua before creating one.**\\r\\n  A folder is a judgment about the relationship, not a filing detail.\\r\\n\\r\\nThen distill exactly as in the live section, steps 1 to 6. The `.docx` stays in\\r\\n`raw/`; what lands in the student folder is what a human wants to read before\\r\\nthe next session.\\r\\n\\r\\nIf the inventory gets a mapping wrong, fix the script or the alias file. Working\\r\\naround it silently means the next session re-derives the same mapping.\\r\\n\\r\\n## Student evidence\\r\\n\\r\\nPT score reports, intake screenshots, homework exports, anything about one\\r\\nstudent that arrives as a file.\\r\\n\\r\\n1. Identify the student (filename, chat context, contents). Ask if unclear.\\r\\n2. Dedupe (above).\\r\\n3. Copy into the student folder under the matching standard subfolder from\\r\\n   `students/README.md`: score reports to `Practice_Test_Reports/`, assigned\\r\\n   work to `Student_Specific_Homework/`, otherwise the folder root with a dated\\r\\n   name. These are raw evidence: read for diagnosis, never edited.\\r\\n4. If it changes a judgment, append the judgment to `teaching-notes.md` with the\\r\\n   file as its cited source.\\r\\n5. Log it.\\r\\n\\r\\n## Bulk exports\\r\\n\\r\\nTakeout and platform dumps land in `raw/data-about-me/` and are git-ignored PII.\\r\\n\\r\\n- Never read one wholesale; it has blown the context window before.\\r\\n- Inventory first (file counts, types, date ranges), report, and let Joshua\\r\\n  pick what matters.\\r\\n- Duplicate exports are common and large. Report duplicates by hash and size;\\r\\n  do not delete without asking.\\r\\n- Analysis across many files goes to a sub-agent that returns a summary, not\\r\\n  file contents.\\r\\n\\r\\n## Hard rules\\r\\n\\r\\n- Never move, delete, or modify original sources. Preserve revisions and hashes.\\r\\n- Never create a student folder without resolving the relationship with Joshua.\\r\\n- Never hand-edit `*.generated.md`; use its owning generator.\\r\\n- Dedupe before ingesting. Distinguish archived from successfully compiled.\\r\\n- Process one source at a time unless batch work is explicitly requested.\\r\\n- Government IDs stay outside this OS. Do not ingest them.\\r\\n- Use the current machine\'s tools and paths, resolved from the vault root.\\r\\n- No email, platform publishing, or assignment is implied by local ingestion.\\r\\n- Read current target contents before changing pages. Automated writes only\\r\\n  modify generated files or fenced generated sections and compare their expected\\r\\n  hash before writing; on a mismatch, re-read and merge instead of overwriting.\\r\\n### example-skill\\r\\n---\\r\\nname: example-skill\\r\\ndescription: This skill should be used when the user asks to \\"demonstrate skills\\", \\"show skill format\\", \\"create a skill template\\", or discusses skill development patterns. Provides a reference template for creating Claude Code plugin skills.\\r\\nversion: 1.0.0\\r\\n---\\r\\n\\r\\n# Example Skill\\r\\n\\r\\nThis skill demonstrates the structure and format for Claude Code plugin skills.\\r\\n\\r\\n## Overview\\r\\n\\r\\nSkills are model-invoked capabilities that Claude autonomously uses based on task context. Unlike commands (user-invoked) or agents (spawned by Claude), skills provide contextual guidance that Claude incorporates into its responses.\\r\\n\\r\\n## When This Skill Applies\\r\\n\\r\\nThis skill activates when the user\'s request involves:\\r\\n- Creating or understanding plugin skills\\r\\n- Skill template or reference needs\\r\\n- Skill development patterns\\r\\n\\r\\n## Skill Structure\\r\\n\\r\\n### Required Files\\r\\n\\r\\n```\\r\\nskills/\\r\\n└── skill-name/\\r\\n    └── SKILL.md          # Main skill definition (required)\\r\\n```\\r\\n\\r\\n### Optional Supporting Files\\r\\n\\r\\n```\\r\\nskills/\\r\\n└── skill-name/\\r\\n    ├── SKILL.md          # Main skill definition\\r\\n    ├── README.md         # Additional documentation\\r\\n    ├── references/       # Reference materials\\r\\n    │   └── patterns.md\\r\\n    ├── examples/         # Example files\\r\\n    │   └── sample.md\\r\\n    └── scripts/          # Helper scripts\\r\\n        └── helper.sh\\r\\n```\\r\\n\\r\\n## Frontmatter Options\\r\\n\\r\\nSkills support these frontmatter fields:\\r\\n\\r\\n- **name** (required): Skill identifier\\r\\n- **description** (required): Trigger conditions - describe when Claude should use this skill\\r\\n- **version** (optional): Semantic version number\\r\\n- **license** (optional): License information or reference\\r\\n\\r\\n## Writing Effective Descriptions\\r\\n\\r\\nThe description field is crucial - it tells Claude when to invoke the skill.\\r\\n\\r\\n**Good description patterns:**\\r\\n```yaml\\r\\ndescription: This skill should be used when the user asks to \\"specific phrase\\", \\"another phrase\\", mentions \\"keyword\\", or discusses topic-area.\\r\\n```\\r\\n\\r\\n**Include:**\\r\\n- Specific trigger phrases users might say\\r\\n- Keywords that indicate relevance\\r\\n- Topic areas the skill covers\\r\\n\\r\\n## Skill Content Guidelines\\r\\n\\r\\n1. **Clear purpose**: State what the skill helps with\\r\\n2. **When to use**: Define activation conditions\\r\\n3. **Structured guidance**: Organize information logically\\r\\n4. **Actionable instructions**: Provide concrete steps\\r\\n5. **Examples**: Include practical examples when helpful\\r\\n\\r\\n## Best Practices\\r\\n\\r\\n- Keep skills focused on a single domain\\r\\n- Write descriptions that clearly indicate when to activate\\r\\n- Include reference materials in subdirectories for complex skills\\r\\n- Test that the skill activates for expected queries\\r\\n- Avoid overlap with other skills\' trigger conditions\\r\\n### brainstorming\\r\\n---\\r\\nname: brainstorming\\r\\ndescription: \\"You MUST use this before any creative work - creating features, building components, adding functionality, or modifying behavior. Explores user intent, requirements and design before implementation.\\"\\r\\n---\\r\\n\\r\\n# Brainstorming Ideas Into Designs\\r\\n\\r\\nHelp turn ideas into fully formed designs and specs through natural collaborative dialogue.\\r\\n\\r\\nStart by understanding the current project context, then ask questions one at a time to refine the idea. Once you understand what you\'re building, present the design and get user approval.\\r\\n\\r\\n<HARD-GATE>\\r\\nDo NOT invoke any implementatio…313 tokens truncated…nt design** — in sections scaled to their complexity, get user approval after each section\\r\\n6. **Write design doc** — save to `docs/superpowers/specs/YYYY-MM-DD-<topic>-design.md` and commit\\r\\n7. **Spec self-review** — quick inline check for placeholders, contradictions, ambiguity, scope (see below)\\r\\n8. **User reviews written spec** — ask user to review the spec file before proceeding\\r\\n9. **Transition to implementation** — invoke writing-plans skill to create implementation plan\\r\\n\\r\\n## Process Flow\\r\\n\\r\\n```dot\\r\\ndigraph brainstorming {\\r\\n    \\"Explore project context\\" [shape=box];\\r\\n    \\"Ask clarifying questions\\" [shape=box];\\r\\n    \\"Propose 2-3 approaches\\" [shape=box];\\r\\n    \\"Present design sections\\" [shape=box];\\r\\n    \\"User approves design?\\" [shape=diamond];\\r\\n    \\"Write design doc\\" [shape=box];\\r\\n    \\"Spec self-review\\\\n(fix inline)\\" [shape=box];\\r\\n    \\"User reviews spec?\\" [shape=diamond];\\r\\n    \\"Invoke writing-plans skill\\" [shape=doublecircle];\\r\\n\\r\\n    \\"Explore project context\\" -> \\"Ask clarifying questions\\";\\r\\n    \\"Ask clarifying questions\\" -> \\"Propose 2-3 approaches\\";\\r\\n    \\"Propose 2-3 approaches\\" -> \\"Present design sections\\";\\r\\n    \\"Present design sections\\" -> \\"User approves design?\\";\\r\\n    \\"User approves design?\\" -> \\"Present design sections\\" [label=\\"no, revise\\"];\\r\\n    \\"User approves design?\\" -> \\"Write design doc\\" [label=\\"yes\\"];\\r\\n    \\"Write design doc\\" -> \\"Spec self-review\\\\n(fix inline)\\";\\r\\n    \\"Spec self-review\\\\n(fix inline)\\" -> \\"User reviews spec?\\";\\r\\n    \\"User reviews spec?\\" -> \\"Write design doc\\" [label=\\"changes requested\\"];\\r\\n    \\"User reviews spec?\\" -> \\"Invoke writing-plans skill\\" [label=\\"approved\\"];\\r\\n}\\r\\n```\\r\\n\\r\\n**The terminal state is invoking writing-plans.** Do NOT invoke frontend-design, mcp-builder, or any other implementation skill. The ONLY skill you invoke after brainstorming is writing-plans.\\r\\n\\r\\n## The Process\\r\\n\\r\\n**Understanding the idea:**\\r\\n\\r\\n- Check out the current project state first (files, docs, recent commits)\\r\\n- Before asking detailed questions, assess scope: if the request describes multiple independent subsystems (e.g., \\"build a platform with chat, file storage, billing, and analytics\\"), flag this immediately. Don\'t spend questions refining details of a project that needs to be decomposed first.\\r\\n- If the project is too large for a single spec, help the user decompose into sub-projects: what are the independent pieces, how do they relate, what order should they be built? Then brainstorm the first sub-project through the normal design flow. Each sub-project gets its own spec → plan → implementation cycle.\\r\\n- For appropriately-scoped projects, ask questions one at a time to refine the idea\\r\\n- Prefer multiple choice questions when possible, but open-ended is fine too\\r\\n- Only one question per message - if a topic needs more exploration, break it into multiple questions\\r\\n- Focus on understanding: purpose, constraints, success criteria\\r\\n\\r\\n**Exploring approaches:**\\r\\n\\r\\n- Propose 2-3 different approaches with trade-offs\\r\\n- Present options conversationally with your recommendation and reasoning\\r\\n- Lead with your recommended option and explain why\\r\\n\\r\\n**Presenting the design:**\\r\\n\\r\\n- Once you believe you understand what you\'re building, present the design\\r\\n- Scale each section to its complexity: a few sentences if straightforward, up to 200-300 words if nuanced\\r\\n- Ask after each section whether it looks right so far\\r\\n- Cover: architecture, components, data flow, error handling, testing\\r\\n- Be ready to go back and clarify if something doesn\'t make sense\\r\\n\\r\\n**Design for isolation and clarity:**\\r\\n\\r\\n- Break the system into smaller units that each have one clear purpose, communicate through well-defined interfaces, and can be understood and tested independently\\r\\n- For each unit, you should be able to answer: what does it do, how do you use it, and what does it depend on?\\r\\n- Can someone understand what a unit does without reading its internals? Can you change the internals without breaking consumers? If not, the boundaries need work.\\r\\n- Smaller, well-bounded units are also easier for you to work with - you reason better about code you can hold in context at once, and your edits are more reliable when files are focused. When a file grows large, that\'s often a signal that it\'s doing too much.\\r\\n\\r\\n**Working in existing codebases:**\\r\\n\\r\\n- Explore the current structure before proposing changes. Follow existing patterns.\\r\\n- Where existing code has problems that affect the work (e.g., a file that\'s grown too large, unclear boundaries, tangled responsibilities), include targeted improvements as part of the design - the way a good developer improves code they\'re working in.\\r\\n- Don\'t propose unrelated refactoring. Stay focused on what serves the current goal.\\r\\n\\r\\n## After the Design\\r\\n\\r\\n**Documentation:**\\r\\n\\r\\n- Write the validated design (spec) to `docs/superpowers/specs/YYYY-MM-DD-<topic>-design.md`\\r\\n  - (User preferences for spec location override this default)\\r\\n- Use elements-of-style:writing-clearly-and-concisely skill if available\\r\\n- Commit the design document to git\\r\\n\\r\\n**Spec Self-Review:**\\r\\nAfter writing the spec document, look at it with fresh eyes:\\r\\n\\r\\n1. **Placeholder scan:** Any \\"TBD\\", \\"TODO\\", incomplete sections, or vague requirements? Fix them.\\r\\n2. **Internal consistency:** Do any sections contradict each other? Does the architecture match the feature descriptions?\\r\\n3. **Scope check:** Is this focused enough for a single implementation plan, or does it need decomposition?\\r\\n4. **Ambiguity check:** Could any requirement be interpreted two different ways? If so, pick one and make it explicit.\\r\\n\\r\\nFix any issues inline. No need to re-review — just fix and move on.\\r\\n\\r\\n**User Review Gate:**\\r\\nAfter the spec review loop passes, ask the user to review the written spec before proceeding:\\r\\n\\r\\n> \\"Spec written and committed to `<path>`. Please review it and let me know if you want to make any changes before we start writing out the implementation plan.\\"\\r\\n\\r\\nWait for the user\'s response. If they request changes, make them and re-run the spec review loop. Only proceed once the user approves.\\r\\n\\r\\n**Implementation:**\\r\\n\\r\\n- Invoke the writing-plans skill to create a detailed implementation plan\\r\\n- Do NOT invoke any other skill. writing-plans is the next step.\\r\\n\\r\\n## Key Principles\\r\\n\\r\\n- **One question at a time** - Don\'t overwhelm with multiple questions\\r\\n- **Multiple choice preferred** - Easier to answer than open-ended when possible\\r\\n- **YAGNI ruthlessly** - Remove unnecessary features from all designs\\r\\n- **Explore alternatives** - Always propose 2-3 approaches before settling\\r\\n- **Incremental validation** - Present design, get approval before moving on\\r\\n- **Be flexible** - Go back and clarify when something doesn\'t make sense\\r\\n\\r\\n## Visual Companion\\r\\n\\r\\nA browser-based companion for showing mockups, diagrams, and visual options during brainstorming. Available as a tool — not a mode. Accepting the companion means it\'s available for questions that benefit from visual treatment; it does NOT mean every question goes through the browser.\\r\\n\\r\\n**Offering the companion (just-in-time):** Do NOT offer it upfront. Wait until a question would genuinely be clearer shown than told — a real mockup / layout / diagram question, not merely a UI *topic*. The first time that happens, offer it then, as its own message:\\r\\n> \\"This next part might be easier if I show you — I can put together mockups, diagrams, and comparisons in a browser tab as we go. It\'s still new and can be token-intensive. Want me to? I\'ll open it for you.\\"\\r\\n\\r\\n**This offer MUST be its own message.** Only the offer — no clarifying question, summary, or other content. Wait for the user\'s response. If they accept, start the server with `--open` so their browser opens to the first screen automatically. If they decline, continue text-only and don\'t offer again unless they raise it.\\r\\n\\r\\n**Per-question decision:** Even after the user accepts, decide FOR EACH QUESTION whether to use the browser or the terminal. The test: **would the user understand this better by seeing it than reading it?**\\r\\n\\r\\n- **Use the browser** for content that IS visual — mockups, wireframes, layout comparisons, architecture diagrams, side-by-side visual designs\\r\\n- **Use the terminal** for content that is text — requirements questions, conceptual choices, tradeoff lists, A/B/C/D text options, scope decisions\\r\\n\\r\\nA question about a UI topic is not automatically a visual question. \\"What does personality mean in this context?\\" is a conceptual question — use the terminal. \\"Which wizard layout works better?\\" is a visual question — use the browser.\\r\\n\\r\\nIf they agree to the companion, read the detailed guide before proceeding:\\r\\n`skills/brainstorming/visual-companion.md`\\r\\n### session-handoff\\r\\n---\\r\\nname: session-handoff\\r\\ndescription: Use when Joshua says \\"session handoff\\", \\"hand off\\", \\"handoff summary\\", \\"summarize before I clear\\", or is about to /clear mid-work (especially near the ~250k dumb-zone). Produces a chat-only handoff — decisions, shipped changes, key files, running state, verification, deferrals, open questions — so a fresh agent (Claude or Codex) continues seamlessly. Distinct from `wrapup`, which updates the wiki ledgers; this writes nothing.\\r\\n---\\r\\n\\r\\n# Session Handoff\\r\\n\\r\\nProduce a repeatable end-of-session summary so Joshua can `/clear` and start a fresh agent without losing continuity. The next agent should pick up by reading this summary alone.\\r\\n\\r\\nThis is a **context-handoff artifact**, not a status report. The audience is a future instance of you, not a stakeholder.\\r\\n\\r\\n**Handoff vs. wrapup:** run `session-handoff` when the *context window* is the problem — nearing ~250k tokens (the dumb zone), or passing work between Claude and Codex. It is chat-only and writes nothing. Run `wrapup` when the *work day* is done — it strikes tasks, refreshes `wiki/hot.md`, and appends `wiki/log.md`. They can be run back to back (wrapup to persist, then handoff to reset).\\r\\n\\r\\n## When to invoke\\r\\n\\r\\nJoshua says: \\"session handoff\\", \\"hand off\\", \\"handoff summary\\", \\"summarize before I clear\\", or any near-equivalent. Note \\"let\'s wrap up\\" belongs to `wrapup`, not here — if he says that and the context window is also deep, run `wrapup` first, then offer this. Also invoke proactively if he says he\'s about to `/clear` without having run it, or if the session is clearly deep into the dumb zone.\\r\\n\\r\\n## How to produce the summary\\r\\n\\r\\n1. **Review the full conversation**, not just the last few turns. Handoffs miss things when they only summarize recent context.\\r\\n2. **Pull state from these sources (in order):**\\r\\n   - Plan files referenced this session (check `~/.claude/plans/` if a plan was mentioned).\\r\\n   - TodoWrite state — any in-progress or pending tasks.\\r\\n   - Background processes started with `run_in_background` — shell IDs are load-bearing for the next agent.\\r\\n   - Files created or modified this session — you know what you touched; don\'t grep to re-discover.\\r\\n   - Memory files written or updated (`~/.claude/projects/C--Users-Joshu-dev-ai-os/memory/`).\\r\\n   - Unresolved questions — things you asked Joshua that never got a clear answer, or things he asked that got deflected.\\r\\n3. **Do NOT audit the filesystem.** This is synthesis of what happened in THIS session. No `git log`, no broad `Glob` sweeps. If you didn\'t touch it this session, it doesn\'t belong here.\\r\\n4. **Produce the output in chat.** Do not write a file. Do not update memory. Chat-only.\\r\\n\\r\\n## Output template — use exactly this structure, every time\\r\\n\\r\\n```\\r\\n# Session Handoff — <one-line title of what this session was about>\\r\\n\\r\\n## Where it started\\r\\n<2-3 sentences: what Joshua asked for, key framing or constraints that emerged>\\r\\n\\r\\n## Decisions locked + what shipped\\r\\n- <decision or change> — <why, and where it lives (absolute path if a file)>\\r\\n- ...\\r\\n\\r\\n## Key files for next session\\r\\n- `<absolute path>` — <why the next agent should read this first>\\r\\n- Plan file: `<path>` (if a plan drove the session)\\r\\n- Memory files touched: `<paths>` (if any)\\r\\n\\r\\n## Running state\\r\\n- Background processes: <shell IDs + what they are + how to kill> — or \\"none\\"\\r\\n- Dev servers / ports: <url + port> — or \\"none\\"\\r\\n- Open worktrees / branches: <paths> — or \\"none\\"\\r\\n\\r\\n## Verified state as of <HH:MM>\\r\\n- <claim about live/system state> — <how it was checked, and when>\\r\\n- <claim> — NOT re-verified this session; last confirmed <when>\\r\\n- ...\\r\\n\\r\\n## Verification — how to confirm things still work\\r\\n- `<command>` — <expected outcome>\\r\\n- ...\\r\\n\\r\\n## Deferred + open questions\\r\\n- Deferred: <item> — <why pushed to later>\\r\\n- OPEN (must be resolved or re-asked before new work): <question needing Joshua\'s input> — <context>\\r\\n\\r\\n## Pick up here\\r\\n<1-2 sentences: the single most likely next action for a fresh agent>\\r\\n```\\r\\n\\r\\n## Hard rules\\r\\n\\r\\n1. **Chat output only.** Never write the handoff to a file. Never update memory from this skill. (That is `wrapup`\'s job, not this one.)\\r\\n2. **Never invent state.** If a section has nothing to report, write \\"none\\" — do not omit the section. Structure stability is the whole point.\\r\\n3. **Absolute paths always.** The next agent may have a different working directory, or be Codex.\\r\\n4. **If a plan file drove the session, name it first** in \\"Key files\\" so the next agent reads it before anything else.\\r\\n5. **No emojis, no hype, no \\"great job\\" summaries.** Terse and concrete — paths, commands, shell IDs, decisions. Tone of a seasoned engineer handing off at end-of-shift.\\r\\n6. **Background process IDs are critical.** If you started any `run_in_background` shells, their IDs must appear in \\"Running state\\" with the kill command — the next agent cannot find them otherwise.\\r\\n7. **Stamp verified state, and separate it from assumed state.** Run `date \\"+%H:%M\\"` and use the real time. Every claim about live systems (deploy status, DB contents, what was sent, what is published) is either something you actually checked this session — say how — or explicitly marked NOT re-verified. A handoff that presents stale belief as current state makes the next session re-derive everything, which is the exact cost this skill exists to remove.\\r\\n8. **Open questions are obligations, not notes.** Anything under OPEN must be resolved by the next session or re-asked to Joshua before it starts new work. Requirements have been silently re-typed across sessions, and a promised artifact once never arrived because nobody re-asked. If a question was open in the handoff you are picking up from, it is the first thing you raise.\\r\\n\\r\\n## Anti-patterns — do not do these\\r\\n\\r\\n- Summarizing the last 3 turns and calling it a handoff.\\r\\n- Listing files by relative path.\\r\\n- Skipping \\"Running state\\" because \\"nothing is running\\" — write \\"none\\" instead.\\r\\n- Writing the summary to any file. This is chat-only by design.\\r\\n- Adding a \\"what went well / what went poorly\\" retrospective. This isn\'t a retro.\\r\\n- Recommending next steps beyond the single \\"Pick up here\\" line. The next agent decides; you just hand off.\\r\\n"}'}]

Use when discussing codebase terminology, writing or editing a GLOSSARY.md, or recording or editing an ADR.\\r\\n---\\r\\n\\r\\n# Domain Modeling\\r\\n\\r\\nActively build and sharpen the project\'s domain model as you design. This is the *active* discipline: challenging terms, inventing edge-case scenarios, and writing the glossary and decisions down the moment they crystallise. (Merely *reading* `GLOSSARY.md` for vocabulary is not this skill: that\'s a one-line habit any skill can do. This skill is for when you\'re changing the model, not just consuming it.)\\r\\n\\r\\n## File structure\\r\\n\\r\\nMost repos have a single context:\\r\\n\\r\\n```\\r\\n/\\r\\n├── GLOSSARY.md\\r\\n├── docs/\\r\\n│   └── adr/\\r\\n│       ├── 0001-event-sourced-orders.md\\r\\n│       └── 0002-postgres-for-write-model.md\\r\\n└── src/\\r\\n```\\r\\n\\r\\nIf a `GLOSSARY-MAP.md` exists at the root, the repo has multiple contexts. The map points to where each one lives:\\r\\n\\r\\n```\\r\\n/\\r\\n├── GLOSSARY-MAP.md\\r\\n├── docs/\\r\\n│   └── adr/                          ← system-wide decisions\\r\\n├── src/\\r\\n│   ├── ordering/\\r\\n│   │   ├── GLOSSARY.md\\r\\n│   │   └── docs/adr/                 ← context-specific decisions\\r\\n│   └── billing/\\r\\n│       ├── GLOSSARY.md\\r\\n│       └── docs/adr/\\r\\n```\\r\\n\\r\\nCreate files lazily: only when you have something to write. If no `GLOSSARY.md` exists, create one when the first term is resolved. If no `docs/adr/` exists, create it when the first ADR is needed.\\r\\n\\r\\n## During the session\\r\\n\\r\\n### Challenge against the glossary\\r\\n\\r\\nWhen the user uses a term that conflicts with the existing language in `GLOSSARY.md`, call it out immediately. \\"Your glossary defines \'cancellation\' as X, but you seem to mean Y. Which is it?\\"\\r\\n\\r\\n### Sharpen fuzzy language\\r\\n\\r\\nWhen the user uses vague or overloaded terms, propose a precise canonical term. \\"You\'re saying \'account\': do you mean the Customer or the User? Those are different things.\\"\\r\\n\\r\\n### Discuss concrete scenarios\\r\\n\\r\\nWhen domain relationships are being discussed, stress-test them with specific scenarios. Invent scenarios that probe edge cases and force the user to be precise about the boundaries between concepts.\\r\\n\\r\\n### Cross-reference with code\\r\\n\\r\\nWhen the user states how something works, check whether the code agrees. If you find a contradiction, surface it: \\"Your code cancels entire Orders, but you just said partial cancellation is possible. Which is right?\\"\\r\\n\\r\\n### Update GLOSSARY.md inline\\r\\n\\r\\nWhen a term is resolved, update `GLOSSARY.md` right there. Don\'t batch these up: capture them as they happen. Use the format in [GLOSSARY-FORMAT.md](./GLOSSARY-FORMAT.md).\\r\\n\\r\\n`GLOSSARY.md` should be totally devoid of implementation details. Do not treat `GLOSSARY.md` as a spec, a scratch pad, or a repository for implementation decisions. It is a glossary and nothing else.\\r\\n\\r\\n### Offer ADRs sparingly\\r\\n\\r\\nOnly offer to create an ADR when all three are true:\\r\\n\\r\\n1. **Hard to reverse**: the cost of changing your mind later is meaningful\\r\\n2. **Surprising without context**: a future reader will wonder \\"why did they do it this way?\\"\\r\\n3. **The result of a real trade-off**: there were genuine alternatives and you picked one for specific reasons\\r\\n\\r\\nIf any of the three is missing, skip the ADR. Use the format in [ADR-FORMAT.md](./ADR-FORMAT.md).\\r\\n### edit-article\\r\\n---\\r\\nname: edit-article\\r\\ndescription: Edit and improve articles by restructuring sections, improving clarity, and tightening prose. Use maximum 240 characters per paragraph.\\r\\n### grill-by-claude\\r\\n---\\r\\nname: grill-by-claude\\r\\ndescription: Grill a plan with Codex, then get independent Claude Code review and revise against its findings. Do not load or restore the upstream legacy implementation.\\r\\n### grilling\\r\\n---\\r\\nname: grilling\\r\\ndescription: Grill the user relentlessly about a plan, decision, or idea. Use when the user wants to stress-test their thinking, or uses any \'grill\' trigger phrases.\\r\\n---\\r\\n\\r\\nInterview the user relentlessly until you reach a shared understanding. Map this as a **design tree**: every decision branches into the decisions that hang off it.\\r\\n\\r\\nWork the tree in **rounds**. The **frontier** is every decision whose prerequisites are already settled: the questions you can ask _now_ without guessing at answers you haven\'t heard yet. Ask the whole frontier in one round: number each question and give your recommended answer. Then wait for the user\'s answers before the next round.\\r\\n\\r\\nFormat a round like so:\\r\\n\\r\\n```\\r\\n❓ **Q1** - **<question title>**: <question body, might be multiple paragraphs, including multiple choices>\\r\\n\\r\\n➡️ <your recommended answer>\\r\\n\\r\\n---\\r\\n\\r\\n❓ **Q2** - **<question title>**: <question body, might be multiple paragraphs, including multiple choices>\\r\\n\\r\\n➡️ <your recommended answer>\\r\\n```\\r\\n\\r\\nWord each question so \\"yes\\" accepts your recommended answer.\\r\\n\\r\\nEach round the user answers reshapes the tree: settled decisions push the frontier outward and unblock questions that depended on them. Recompute the frontier and ask the next round. A question whose answer depends on another question still open in this round belongs to a _later_ round, not this one.\\r\\n\\r\\nFinding _facts_ is your job, never the user\'s. When a frontier question needs a fact from the environment (filesystem, tools, etc.), dispatch a sub-agent to find it; don\'t ask the user for anything you could look up yourself. Don\'t block on it: a running exploration is an unsettled prerequisite, so only the questions downstream of it wait for the sub-agent to report; ask the rest of the frontier now. The _decisions_ are the user\'s: put each to them and wait.\\r\\n\\r\\nThe session is done when the frontier is empty: every branch of the design tree visited, nothing left silently assumed. Do not act on it until the user confirms you have reached a shared understanding.\\r\\n### implement\\r\\n---\\r\\nname: implement\\r\\ndescription: \\"Implement a piece of work based on a spec or set of tickets.\\"\\r\\ndisable-model-invocation: true\\r\\n---\\r\\n\\r\\nImplement the work described by the user in the spec or tickets.\\r\\n\\r\\nIf the user passes a ticket reference, fetch it from the issue tracker and state its title before starting. If the reference is ambiguous, ask.\\r\\n\\r\\nCall the Skill tool with \\"tdd\\" where possible, at pre-agreed seams.\\r\\n\\r\\nRun typechecking regularly, single test files regularly, and the full test suite once at the end.\\r\\n\\r\\nOnce done, call the Skill tool with \\"code-review\\" to review the work.\\r\\n\\r\\nCommit your work to the current branch.\\r\\n### implement-spec\\r\\n---\\r\\nname: implement-spec\\r\\ndescription: \\"Implement the result of /to-spec and /to-tickets in code.\\"\\r\\ndisable-model-invocation: true\\r\\n---\\r\\n\\r\\nYou have been provided a spec. If not, tell the user to run `/setup-matt-pocock-skills`.\\r\\n\\r\\nThe goal is the entire spec implemented on a single **integration branch**, with every ticket resolved the way the issue tracker closes work.\\r\\n\\r\\nThe tickets are not a list of steps. They are a **task graph** with blocking relationships between them. This means there is always a **frontier** of tickets which are ready to be grabbed.\\r\\n\\r\\nCommunication to and from subagents should be sparse. Communicate primarily through **context pointers**: to the spec, tickets, research notes, and previous commits. Don\'t duplicate information already available via pointers.\\r\\n\\r\\n**Implementer subagents** should be run in the background where possible for maximum concurrency.\\r\\n\\r\\n## Steps\\r\\n\\r\\n1. Read the spec and tickets to understand the task graph.\\r\\n\\r\\n2. (optional) Use an **exploration subagent** to conduct any explo…3618 tokens truncated… # every LR slot in the bank\\r\\npython <vault>/system/scripts/lsatlab-pull/crawl_public.py --pts 113  # one test\\r\\n```\\r\\n~4,000 pages, 6 workers, resumable (skips slots already in `data/public/`). Run it in the background. Delete `data/public/` to force a refresh.\\r\\n\\r\\n## 3. Pull the database (read-only)\\r\\n\\r\\n```bash\\r\\npython system/scripts/lsatlab-pull/db_pull.py   # from the vault root; writes data/db/\\r\\n```\\r\\n\\r\\n## 4. Audit\\r\\n\\r\\n```bash\\r\\npython <vault>/system/scripts/lsatlab-pull/audit_bank.py --db <vault>/system/scripts/lsatlab-pull/data/db --out <report.md>\\r\\n```\\r\\nFindings: `key_mismatch` (bank / database / LSAT Lab disagree), `stimulus_not_on_lsatlab` / `stem_not_on_lsatlab` / `choice_not_on_lsatlab` (wrong or damaged question text), `db_stimulus_not_on_lsatlab`, `in_lsatlab_not_in_bank` / `in_bank_not_in_lsatlab_list` (missing or extra slots), `lsatlab_explained_lsatu_not` (LSAT Lab has a written explanation where LSAT U\'s Coverage State is not Complete), `labels_differ`.\\r\\n\\r\\nRead a sample of every finding type before reporting it. Text checks compare normalized prefixes, so a hit can be a formatting difference; say which you confirmed.\\r\\n\\r\\n## 5. Fix\\r\\n\\r\\n- **Labels:** `tag_bank.py --slots ... | --slots-file ... | --missing`, then `node scripts/build-question-bank.mjs`. LSAT Lab\'s current tags win (Joshua, 2026-09-27). Never touches question type.\\r\\n- **Wrong question in a slot:** the database text is usually right. Confirm on the LSAT Lab page, then rebuild the slot: stimulus + stem + key from the database, choices from the PDF. See `corpus/lr-explanations/fixes/` for the 2026-09-27 repair.\\r\\n- **Answer keys:** a disagreement goes to Joshua before anything changes (\\"I think this question is marked wrong\\"), with the three sources side by side.\\r\\n- **Explanations:** database edits go through a snapshot in `raw/sources/lsatu-lr-snapshots/` first, then Lovable `query_database`.\\r\\n- Ship: PR, merge when Joshua says, then `deploy_project` (free) and confirm the change on lsatprep.study by fetching the file.\\r\\n\\r\\n## Record\\r\\n\\r\\nAppend findings to `corpus/lr-explanations/fixes/index.md` and a line to `wiki/log.md`.\\r\\n### lsat-u-platform-actions\\r\\n---\\r\\nname: lsat-u-platform-actions\\r\\ndescription: Operate LSAT U from AI OS. Assign complete interactive Classroom lessons directly through the local lsat-u-lessons MCP server, verify the saved content and student visibility headlessly, and log the assignment. Use the Node CLI for other supported actions.\\r\\n---\\r\\n\\r\\nFor drills, messages, student data, access, signups, due dates, unassign, and unsend, use `assign-lsatu-work`. On Windows, invoke its Node entry point directly instead of relying on Bash being on PATH.\\r\\n\\r\\n\\r\\n# LSAT U Platform Actions\\r\\n\\r\\nJoshua\'s workplace is this brain workspace. LSAT U operations should run headlessly when a supported tool exists. The browser is for checking what a person sees.\\r\\n\\r\\n## Mechanism\\r\\n\\r\\nFor an interactive HTML lesson, call the `lsat-u-lessons` MCP tool `publish_interactive_lesson` with the student\'s exact email, absolute HTML path, and title. The local stdio server is `system/scripts/lsatu-lesson-mcp.mjs`; Codex registration is `lsat-u-lessons`. It calls `system/scripts/lsatu-admin.mjs post-lesson`, which authenticates with the existing admin credentials, posts through `mcp_post_classroom_note`, verifies the saved HTML exactly and student visibility, and then archives only earlier versions with the same lesson marker. A repeat of the current version returns the same item without another notification. Use `dry_run: true` when the student or replacement is uncertain; otherwise publish in one call. MCP tools newly registered during a session may only appear in a new Codex session; the direct Node command is the immediate fallback.\\r\\n\\r\\nThe HTML must be a complete document inside AI OS, under 500 KB, with `<meta name=\\"lsatu-interactive-lesson\\" content=\\"unique-lesson-id\\">`. Reuse the same lesson ID for revisions of that lesson; use a different ID for a different lesson. Inline the CSS, JavaScript, fonts, and visual assets. Preflight rejects nonembedded resources; do not bypass it or paste HTML into an ordinary sanitized note. The already-live Classroom renderer loads marked HTML in a sandboxed iframe with scripts and forms enabled. **Daily lesson posting is a content operation and never requires Lovable.** Only an actual app renderer change follows the separate app deployment rules.\\r\\n\\r\\nRoutine verification is headless: the publisher reads the new item back, compares its HTML byte for byte, checks that it is visible to the intended student, and confirms one active version. The result includes its route and SHA-256. Use Codex\'s in-app browser only when a visual or interaction defect is suspected or the page design or renderer changed. A teacher login cannot open another student\'s `/classroom/item/<id>` route directly. Do not claim a student-session visual check unless one was actually performed.\\r\\n\\r\\nThe student opens the full lesson from Classroom **Notes and recaps**, the in-app notification, or its Inbox link. Classroom Home may show a recent note as a “Read” row, but it has a four-row limit shared with urgent work, so do not promise that every assigned note stays on Home. This does not affect the note\'s visibility in Notes and recaps or its direct item route.\\r\\n\\r\\n## UI fallback routing\\r\\n\\r\\nThe current student verification route is `/teacher/students/<student-id>/notes`. Its “Posted to their Classroom” section shows active notes and labels archived notes as hidden from the student. Use the browser\'s normal controls for any unsupported action, then verify the saved state through a fresh read. In Codex, use the in-app browser, not Chrome. Do not rely on old `/teacher?ws=` routes or old browser-tool names.\\r\\n\\r\\n## Order of operations (every action)\\r\\n\\r\\n1. **Identify the student** exactly (roster names include email; ambiguity → one\\r\\n   concise clarifying question). Check `students/<name>/` for context and\\r\\n   `assignment-log.md` to avoid repeats.\\r\\n2. **Do the action** through MCP or the headless Node CLI when supported. Use the UI fallback only for unsupported actions.\\r\\n3. **Verify it landed**: use the publisher\'s read-after-write result to confirm exact HTML, student visibility, and one active copy of this lesson ID. It archives earlier versions of that ID and leaves unrelated same-title notes alone. Check notifications where available. If verification fails, inspect current items before retrying; never blindly post twice.\\r\\n4. **Log it**: append to `students/<name>/assignment-log.md` (create if missing) with\\r\\n   date, action, item, and evidence; drill verifications also go to\\r\\n   `wiki/guided-drill-verification-log.md`.\\r\\n\\r\\n## Guardrails\\r\\n\\r\\n- Every action here hits **real students on prod**. Anything a student will see\\r\\n  (message text, homework instructions, note bodies) is written in Joshua\'s voice —\\r\\n  route through `wiki/teaching-voice.md`.\\r\\n- If Joshua\'s request fully specifies the action (\\"assign Lydia the conditional\\r\\n  drill\\"), execute without re-asking. If content is open-ended (a message body he\\r\\n  hasn\'t dictated), draft it and show him before sending.\\r\\n- Fail closed: if verification is ambiguous, say exactly what was and wasn\'t\\r\\n  confirmed. Never report an action complete on the strength of a click alone.\\r\\n- No student-facing action as a side effect of a different request.\\r\\n### lsat-u-voice\\r\\n---\\r\\nname: lsat-u-voice\\r\\ndescription: Draft, revise, or calibrate LSAT teaching material using Joshua\'s selected voice standard. Use for lessons, notes, explanations, drills, quizzes, flashcards, and instructional feedback. Logistics emails and marketing use their separate canonical registers.\\r\\n---\\r\\n\\r\\n# Write LSAT material in Joshua\'s selected teaching voice\\r\\n\\r\\nResolve the canonical ai-os vault from the workspace instructions. This project-owned skill takes precedence over older vendor skills with the same name that prescribe a writer blend.\\r\\n\\r\\nBefore drafting or revising, read:\\r\\n\\r\\n1. [Canonical teaching voice](../../../wiki/teaching-voice.md), especially the teaching-content register.\\r\\n2. [LSAT teaching voice standard](../../../references/lsat-teaching-voice-standard.md). Read it in full when calibrating the voice; for subsequent revisions, revisit the relevant sections and examples.\\r\\n3. [Demonstrated copy corrections](../../../wiki/COPY-CORRECTIONS.md).\\r\\n\\r\\nThe detailed standard is maintained in one place. Do not copy it into this skill or replace it with generic brevity rules, required catchphrases, humor quotas, or a fixed number of sentences per paragraph.\\r\\n\\r\\nEstablish the actual lesson topic, prerequisites, evidence, and Joshua\'s approved method. The conditional reference teaches how to explain; it does not add conditional content to another topic. Preserve complete ideas, logical strength, modality, and the selected scope.\\r\\n\\r\\nUse original intuitive examples. Explain the ordinary meaning before notation, show the intermediate reasoning, and give questions a real instructional job. Keep the teacher and reader thinking together. When useful, show a tempting interpretation and how its meaning fails. Fresh practice should require the taught skill and provide reasoned feedback.\\r\\n\\r\\nRead the draft aloud, check its inferences and boundaries, and apply the standard\'s review rubric. Review actual prompt/reveal states when writing for an interactive surface. Do not claim an identical voice has been objectively established; use Joshua\'s corrections to refine calibration.\\r\\n\\r\\nThis skill governs local authoring. Posting, sending, assigning, deploying, or generating paid media requires the authorization and workflow appropriate to that action.\\r\\n### lovable-prompt\\r\\n---\\r\\nname: lovable-prompt\\r\\ndescription: Produce a short, paste-ready prompt for Lovable when a change can only happen through the Lovable UI (not code Claude Code can reach directly, not a Supabase migration). Use when Joshua asks \\"give me the prompt for Lovable\\", \\"what do I send Lovable\\", or a task turns out to require Lovable-side config/UI action. Trigger with /lovable-prompt.\\r\\n---\\r\\n\\r\\nProduce a short, paste-ready prompt for Lovable\'s chat, for the residual class of changes Claude Code cannot reach directly.\\r\\n\\r\\n## When this applies\\r\\n\\r\\nBefore reaching for this, check whether the task is actually reachable another way:\\r\\n- **Schema/data change** → use the Supabase MCP tools directly (`apply_migration`, `execute_sql` with `confirm_cost`). Do not hand this to Lovable.\\r\\n- **Code change in the repo** → make it directly and push via `.claude/safe-push.sh` (see LSATU CLAUDE.md). Do not hand this to Lovable.\\r\\n- Only fall back to a Lovable prompt for things genuinely gated behind the Lovable UI/platform itself: project-level settings, Lovable\'s own deploy/preview config, or when Joshua explicitly wants Lovable\'s agent to do the implementation instead of Claude Code.\\r\\n\\r\\n## Output format\\r\\n\\r\\nJoshua\'s preference (from repeated corrections: \\"cosie short promts\\" / concise short prompts): **short**, in a fenced code block, no preamble inside the block, one task per prompt unless he asked for a batch.\\r\\n\\r\\n```\\r\\n[imperative, 1-3 sentences: exactly what to change, plaintext, no markdown inside the block]\\r\\n```\\r\\n\\r\\nAbove the code block, in plain text (not in the block):\\r\\n- One line on why this needs to go through Lovable rather than being done directly.\\r\\n- Anything Joshua should verify after Lovable applies it.\\r\\n\\r\\n## Rules\\r\\n\\r\\n- No em dashes.\\r\\n- Never pad the prompt with context Lovable doesn\'t need (file structure explanations, rationale) — Lovable prompts are terse instructions, not briefs.\\r\\n- If the change touches product rules in the LSATU CLAUDE.md (Foyer/Mainhub nav, granular feature flags, no fake data, etc.), restate the relevant constraint inside the prompt so Lovable doesn\'t violate it.\\r\\n### research\\r\\n---\\r\\nname: research\\r\\ndescription: Investigate a question against high-trust primary sources and capture the findings as a Markdown file in the repo. Use when the user wants a topic researched, docs or API facts gathered, or reading legwork delegated to a background agent.\\r\\n---\\r\\n\\r\\nSpin up a **background agent** to do the research, so you keep working while it reads.\\r\\n\\r\\nIts job:\\r\\n\\r\\n1. Investigate the question against **primary sources** (official docs, source code, specs, first-party APIs), not a secondary write-up of them. Follow every claim back to the source that owns it.\\r\\n2. Write the findings to a single Markdown file, citing each claim\'s source.\\r\\n3. Save it where the repo already keeps such notes; match the existing convention, and if there is none, put it somewhere sensible and say where.\\r\\n### resolving-merge-conflicts\\r\\n---\\r\\nname: resolving-merge-conflicts\\r\\ndescription: \\"Use when you need to resolve an in-progress git merge/rebase conflict.\\"\\r\\n---\\r\\n\\r\\n1. **See the current state** of the merge/rebase. Check git history, and the conflicting files.\\r\\n\\r\\n2. **Find the primary sources** for each conflict. Understand deeply why each change was made, and what the original intent was. Read the commit messages, check the PRs, check original issues/tickets.\\r\\n\\r\\n3. **Resolve each hunk.** Preserve both intents where possible. If rebasing, continue the rebase process until all commits are rebased.\\r\\n### wait-what\\r\\n---\\r\\nname: wait-what\\r\\ndescription: \\"Stop. Then: mark the vault build page complete, strike the tasks.md item, log it, and give Joshua the shipped summary (route, module list, anything deferred to v1.5).\\r\\n\\r\\n## What this skill does NOT do\\r\\n\\r\\n- Never modifies main-conclusion or other bootcamps\' files.\\r\\n- Never claims sufficiency the audit didn\'t show.\\r\\n- Never skips a gate or proceeds past one without Joshua\'s explicit approval.\\r\\n- Never invents structure or theme beyond the Intro to LR template without an approved deviation.\\r\\n### booking-link\\r\\n---\\r\\nname: booking-link\\r\\ndescription: Use whenever Joshua wants a one-off booking link for LSAT U — \\"make me a link for Dakota at 7:15 tomorrow\\", \\"send her a link to book tonight\\", \\"one-off link, $60\\", \\"short notice link\\", \\"I need a link she can schedule herself with\\". Mints a single-use URL that sells exactly one session at a price you set, optionally pinned to one exact time, and closes after she books. Also covers listing and revoking existing links.\\r\\n---\\r\\n\\r\\n# One-off booking links\\r\\n\\r\\nA URL Joshua sends to one person. She opens it, books one session, pays, and\\r\\ngets the Google Meet invite from the ordinary booking flow. Then the link\\r\\ncloses.\\r\\n\\r\\n## Authorization\\r\\n\\r\\nMinting a link is pre-authorized. Joshua asking for a link means make it now —\\r\\ndo not ask permission, ask only for the facts you actually need.\\r\\n\\r\\n**Never send the link anywhere.** Print it and hand it to Joshua. He decides who\\r\\ngets it. A link is a Bearer [REDACTED]: whoever holds it can book that slot.\\r\\n\\r\\n## What you need before running\\r\\n\\r\\nOnly two things are required, and one has a default:\\r\\n\\r\\n- **Price** in dollars. Required — links always charge, and the standard rate is\\r\\n  $45 but a given person may pay something else. Ask if it was not said.\\r\\n- **Who it is for.** Used only for the admin-side note, never in the URL. If\\r\\n  Joshua did not say, use a short description.\\r\\n\\r\\nEverything else is optional. Ask for nothing you were not given.\\r\\n\\r\\n## Running it\\r\\n\\r\\nFrom `~/ai-os-projects/lsatu`:\\r\\n\\r\\n```bash\\r\\nnpm run booking:link -- --for \\"Dakota\\" --price 45 --at \\"2026-09-10 19:15\\"\\r\\n```\\r\\n\\r\\nTimes in `--at` are wall-clock in Joshua\'s booking timezone (`America/Toronto`),\\r\\nformat `YYYY-MM-DD HH:mm`, 24-hour. Convert \\"7:15pm tomorrow\\" yourself — resolve\\r\\nrelative dates against today before running, and never pass a relative word\\r\\nthrough.\\r\\n\\r\\nIt prints the URL, the price, the time, and how many times the link can sell.\\r\\nGive Joshua the URL exactly as printed.\\r\\n\\r\\n### The flags\\r\\n\\r\\n| Flag | Default | What it does |\\r\\n|---|---|---|\\r\\n| `--for` | — | Who the link is for. Note only, never in the URL. |\\r\\n| `--price` | — | Dollars. Required. |\\r\\n| `--at` | none | Pin one exact time. See below. |\\r\\n| `--minutes` | 70 | Session length. |\\r\\n| `--notice` | 1440, or 0 with `--at` | Minimum notice in minutes. `0` means \\"bookable right now\\". |\\r\\n| `--window` | 6 | How many business days ahead the picker reaches. |\\r\\n| `--label` | \\"LSAT Session\\" | The title she sees on the page. |\\r\\n| `--note` | auto | Admin reminder of who and why. |\\r\\n\\r\\n### Pinned versus picker\\r\\n\\r\\n**`--at` pins one time.** She sees only that time and confirms it. The minimum\\r\\nnotice, the rolling window and the weekly hours are all skipped, because Joshua\\r\\nchoosing the time *is* that decision. This is the right shape for \\"I have a gap\\r\\nat 7:15 tonight, let her take it.\\"\\r\\n\\r\\n**Without `--at` she gets a calendar** of open times, still inside the weekly\\r\\nhours. Use `--notice 0` for a short-notice link she can book today, and\\r\\n`--window` to control how far ahead it reaches.\\r\\n\\r\\nDouble-booking is never skipped either way. A pinned time that clashes with\\r\\nsomething already on the calendar is refused at mint time — the script deletes\\r\\nthe link and tells you what it hit — and refused again inside the booking\\r\\ntransaction.\\r\\n\\r\\n## Listing and revoking\\r\\n\\r\\n```bash\\r\\nnpm run booking:link -- --list\\r\\nnpm run booking:link -- --revoke <slug>\\r\\n```\\r\\n\\r\\n`--list` shows every one-off link with its state: `open`, `used`, or `revoked`.\\r\\nRevoking is immediate and the URL stops resolving.\\r\\n\\r\\n## Reading the outcome honestly\\r\\n\\r\\n- **\\"clashes with something already on your calendar\\"** — the time is taken. No\\r\\n  link was created. Tell Joshua what he asked for is not free and offer to pick\\r\\n  another time; do not silently mint a different one.\\r\\n- **\\"would have no open times at all\\"** — a picker link whose window and weekly\\r\\n  hours produce nothing. Usually `--window` is too small or the hours are empty.\\r\\n- **A time in the past** is refused. If Joshua asks for a time that has already\\r\\n  gone by today, say so rather than rolling it to tomorrow on your own.\\r\\n\\r\\n## How it works, so you can debug it\\r\\n\\r\\nA one-off link is a row in `booking_event_types` with a random 10-character slug\\r\\nand `single_use` set. That is the same table defining the ordinary session and\\r\\nthe consultation, and every layer beneath — the page, the `single-session` edge\\r\\nfunction, the SQL slot policy, the claim transaction — is already keyed by event\\r\\nslug. So the link books through exactly the code a normal session books through.\\r\\nThere is no second booking path to keep in sync.\\r\\n\\r\\nSingle use is enforced by the `enforce_booking_event_shape` trigger under a\\r\\nper-slug advisory lock, so two people opening the same link at the same moment\\r\\ncannot both get through. A hold holds the link; letting the checkout expire\\r\\nreleases it; a cancelled or refunded booking stays spent, and a replacement\\r\\nneeds a fresh link.\\r\\n\\r\\nRelevant files:\\r\\n\\r\\n- `scripts/booking-link.ts` — the CLI\\r\\n- `src/pages/OneOffBooking.tsx` and the `/book/x/:slug` route in `src/App.tsx`\\r\\n- `supabase/migrations/20260908120000_one_off_booking_links.sql`\\r\\n- `supabase/functions/single-session/index.ts`\\r\\n\\r\\n## Credentials\\r\\n\\r\\n`LSATPREP_ADMIN_EMAIL` / `LSATPREP_ADMIN_PASSWORD` from `~/ai-os/.env`, which is\\r\\ngit-ignored. [{'type': 'input_text', 'text': 'Script completed\nWall time 10.8 seconds\nOutput:\n'}, {'type': 'input_text', 'text': '{"chunk_id":"a2cca9","wall_time_seconds":0.4281215,"exit_code":0,"original_token_count":3153,"output":"---\\r\\nname: watch\\r\\ndescription: Watch a video (URL or local path). Downloads with yt-dlp, extracts auto-scaled frames with ffmpeg, pulls the transcript from captions (or Whisper API fallback), and hands the result to Claude so it can answer questions about what\'s in the video.\\r\\nargument-hint: \\"<video-url-or-path> [question]\\"\\r\\nallowed-tools: Bash, Read, AskUserQuestion\\r\\nhomepage: https://github.com/bradautomates/claude-video\\r\\nrepository: https://github.com/bradautomates/claude-video\\r\\nauthor: bradautomates\\r\\nlicense: MIT\\r\\nuser-invocable: true\\r\\n---\\r\\n\\r\\n# /watch — Claude watches a video\\r\\n\\r\\nYou don\'t have a video input; this skill gives you one. A Python script downloads the video, extracts frames as JPEGs, gets a timestamped transcript (native captions first, then Whisper API as fallback), and prints frame paths. You then `Read` each frame path to see the images and combine them with the transcript to answer the user.\\r\\n\\r\\n## Step 0 — Setup preflight (runs every `/watch` invocation, silent on success)\\r\\n\\r\\n**Python interpreter:** every `python3 ...` command in this skill is for macOS/Linux. On **Windows**, substitute `python` — the `python3` command on Windows is the Microsoft Store stub and will not run the script.\\r\\n\\r\\nBefore every `/watch` run, verify that dependencies and an API key are in place:\\r\\n\\r\\n```bash\\r\\npython3 \\"${CLAUDE_SKILL_DIR}/scripts/setup.py\\" --check\\r\\n```\\r\\n\\r\\nThis is a <100ms lookup. On exit 0, the script emits **nothing** — proceed to Step 1 without comment. **Do NOT announce \\"setup is complete\\" to the user** — they don\'t need a status message on every turn. The only acceptable user-visible output from Step 0 is when remediation is required.\\r\\n\\r\\nOn non-zero exit, follow the table:\\r\\n\\r\\n| Exit | Meaning | Action |\\r\\n|------|---------|--------|\\r\\n| `2` | Missing binaries (`ffmpeg` / `ffprobe` / `yt-dlp`) | Run installer |\\r\\n| `3` | No Whisper API key | Run installer to scaffold `.env`, then ask user for a key |\\r\\n| `4` | Both missing | Run installer, then ask for a key |\\r\\n\\r\\nThe installer is idempotent — safe to re-run:\\r\\n\\r\\n```bash\\r\\npython3 \\"${CLAUDE_SKILL_DIR}/scripts/setup.py\\"\\r\\n```\\r\\n\\r\\nOn macOS with Homebrew, it auto-installs `ffmpeg` and `yt-dlp`. On Linux/Windows, it prints the exact install commands for the user to run. It scaffolds `~/.config/watch/.env` with commented placeholders at `0600` perms, and writes `SETUP_COMPLETE=true` once deps + a key are in place so the next session knows this user has already been through the wizard.\\r\\n\\r\\n**If an API key is still missing after install:** use `AskUserQuestion` to ask the user whether they have a Groq API key (preferred — cheaper, faster) or an OpenAI key. Then write it into `~/.config/watch/.env` — set the matching `GROQ_API_KEY=...` or `OPENAI_API_KEY=...` line. If they don\'t want to set up Whisper, proceed with `--no-whisper` and tell them videos without native captions will come back frames-only.\\r\\n\\r\\n**Structured mode (optional):** `python3 \\"${CLAUDE_SKILL_DIR}/scripts/setup.py\\" --json` emits `{status, first_run, missing_binaries, whisper_backend, has_api_key, config_file, platform}` where `status` is one of `ready | needs_install | needs_key | needs_install_and_key`. Use this when you need to branch on specifics (e.g. \\"is this the user\'s very first run?\\" → `first_run: true`).\\r\\n\\r\\nWithin a single session, you can skip Step 0 on follow-up `/watch` calls — once `--check` returned 0, nothing about the environment changes between turns.\\r\\n\\r\\n## When to use\\r\\n\\r\\n- User pastes a video URL (YouTube, Vimeo, X, TikTok, Twitch clip, most yt-dlp-supported sites) and asks about it.\\r\\n- User points at a local video file (`.mp4`, `.mov`, `.mkv`, `.webm`, etc.) and asks about it.\\r\\n- User types `/watch <url-or-path> [question]`.\\r\\n\\r\\n## Recommended limits\\r\\n\\r\\n- **Best accuracy: videos under 10 minutes.** Frame coverage scales inversely with duration.\\r\\n- **Hard caps: 100 frames total and 2 fps.** Token cost grows with frame count, so the script targets a frame budget by duration (and never exceeds 2 fps even when the budget would imply more):\\r\\n  - ≤30s → ~1-2 fps (up to 30 frames)\\r\\n  - 30s-1min → ~40 frames\\r\\n  - 1-3min → ~60 frames\\r\\n  - 3-10min → ~80 frames\\r\\n  - \\\\>10min → 100 frames, sparsely spaced (warning printed)\\r\\n- If the user hands you a long video, consider asking whether they want a specific section before burning tokens on a sparse scan.\\r\\n\\r\\n## How to invoke\\r\\n\\r\\n**Step 1 — parse the user input.** Separate the video source (URL or path) from any question the user asked. Example: `/watch https://youtu.be/abc what language is this in?` → source = `https://youtu.be/abc`, question = `what language is this in?`.\\r\\n\\r\\n**Step 2 — run the watch script.** Pass the source verbatim. Do not shell-escape it yourself beyond normal quoting:\\r\\n\\r\\n```bash\\r\\npython3 \\"${CLAUDE_SKILL_DIR}/scripts/watch.py\\" \\"<source>\\"\\r\\n```\\r\\n\\r\\nOptional flags:\\r\\n- `--start T` / `--end T` — focus on a section. Accepts `SS`, `MM:SS`, or `HH:MM:SS`. When either is set, fps auto-scales denser (see \\"Focusing on a section\\" below).\\r\\n- `--max-frames N` — lower the cap for tighter token budget (e.g. `--max-frames 40`)\\r\\n- `--resolution W` — change frame width in px (default 512; bump to 1024 only if the user needs to read on-screen text)\\r\\n- `--fps F` — override auto-fps (clamped to 2 fps max)\\r\\n- `--out-dir DIR` — keep working files somewhere specific (default: an auto-generated tmp dir)\\r\\n- `--whisper groq|openai` — force a specific Whisper backend (default: prefer Groq if both keys exist)\\r\\n- `--no-whisper` — disable the Whisper fallback entirely (frames-only if no captions)\\r\\n\\r\\n### Focusing on a section (higher frame rate)\\r\\n\\r\\nWhen the user asks about a specific moment — \\"what happens at the 2 minute mark?\\", \\"zoom into 0:45 to 1:00\\", \\"the first 10 seconds\\" — pass `--start` and/or `--end`. The script switches to focused-mode budgets, which are denser than full-video budgets (still capped at 2 fps):\\r\\n\\r\\n- ≤5s → 2 fps (up to 10 frames)\\r\\n- 5-15s → 2 fps (up to 30 frames)\\r\\n- 15-30s → ~2 fps (up to 60 frames)\\r\\n- 30-60s → ~1.3 fps (up to 80 frames)\\r\\n- 60-180s → ~0.6 fps (100 frames, capped)\\r\\n\\r\\nFocused mode is the right call for:\\r\\n- Any moment/range the user names explicitly (\\"around 2:30\\", \\"the intro\\", \\"the last 30 seconds\\").\\r\\n- Any video longer than ~10 minutes where the user\'s question is about a specific part — running focused on the relevant section is far more useful than a sparse scan of the whole thing.\\r\\n- Re-runs after a full scan didn\'t have enough detail in some region.\\r\\n\\r\\nTranscript is auto-filtered to the same range. Frame timestamps are absolute (real video timeline, not offset-from-start).\\r\\n\\r\\nExamples:\\r\\n```bash\\r\\n# Last 10 seconds of a 1 minute video\\r\\npython3 \\"${CLAUDE_SKILL_DIR}/scripts/watch.py\\" video.mp4 --start 50 --end 60\\r\\n\\r\\n# Zoom into 2:15 → 2:45 at 3 fps (90 frames)\\r\\npython3 \\"${CLAUDE_SKILL_DIR}/scripts/watch.py\\" \\"$URL\\" --start 2:15 --end 2:45 --fps 3\\r\\n\\r\\n# From 1h12m to the end of the video\\r\\npython3 \\"${CLAUDE_SKILL_DIR}/scripts/watch.py\\" \\"$URL\\" --start 1:12:00\\r\\n```\\r\\n\\r\\n**Step 3 — Read every frame path the script lists.** The Read tool renders JPEGs directly as images for you. Read all frames in a single message (parallel tool calls) so you see them together. The frames are in chronological order with a `t=MM:SS` timestamp so you can align them to the transcript.\\r\\n\\r\\n**Step 4 — answer the user.** You now have two streams of evidence:\\r\\n- **Frames** — what\'s on screen at each timestamp\\r\\n- **Transcript** — what\'s said at each timestamp. The report\'s header shows the source (`captions` = yt-dlp pulled native subs; `whisper (groq)` or `whisper (openai)` = transcribed by API).\\r\\n\\r\\nIf the user asked a specific question, answer it directly citing timestamps. If they didn\'t ask anything, summarize what happens in the video — structure, key moments, notable visuals, spoken content.\\r\\n\\r\\n**Step 5 — clean up.** The script prints a working directory at the end. If the user isn\'t going to ask follow-ups about this video, delete it with `rm -rf <dir>`. If they might, leave it in place.\\r\\n\\r\\n## Transcription\\r\\n\\r\\nThe script gets a timestamped transcript in one of two ways:\\r\\n\\r\\n1. **Native captions (free, preferred).** yt-dlp pulls manual or auto-generated subtitles from the source platform if available.\\r\\n2. **Whisper API fallback.** If no captions came back (or the source is a local file), the script extracts audio (`ffmpeg -vn -ac 1 -ar 16000 -b:a 64k`, ~0.5 MB/min) and uploads it to whichever Whisper API has a key configured:\\r\\n   - **Groq** — `whisper-large-v3`. Preferred default: cheaper, faster. Get a key at console.groq.com/keys.\\r\\n   - **OpenAI** — `whisper-1`. Fallback. Get a key at platform.openai.com/api-keys.\\r\\n\\r\\nBoth keys live in `~/.config/watch/.env`. The script prefers Groq when both are set; override with `--whisper openai` to force OpenAI. Use `--no-whisper` to skip the fallback entirely.\\r\\n\\r\\n## Failure modes and handling\\r\\n\\r\\n- **Setup preflight failed** → run `python3 \\"${CLAUDE_SKILL_DIR}/scripts/setup.py\\"` (auto-installs ffmpeg/yt-dlp via brew on macOS, scaffolds the `.env`). For API key, ask the user via `AskUserQuestion` and write it to `~/.config/watch/.env`.\\r\\n- **No transcript available** → captions missing AND (no Whisper key OR Whisper API failed). Script prints a hint pointing to setup. Proceed frames-only and tell the user.\\r\\n- **Long video warning printed** → acknowledge it in your answer. Offer to re-run focused on a specific section via `--start`/`--end` rather than a sparse full-video scan.\\r\\n- **Download fails** → yt-dlp\'s error goes to stderr. If it\'s a login-required or region-locked video, tell the user plainly; do not keep retrying.\\r\\n- **Whisper request fails** → the error is printed to stderr (likely: invalid key, rate limit, or 25 MB upload limit on a very long video). The report will say \\"none available\\" for transcript. You can retry with `--whisper openai` if Groq failed (or vice versa).\\r\\n\\r\\n## Token efficiency\\r\\n\\r\\nThis skill burns tokens primarily on frames. Order of magnitude:\\r\\n- 80 frames at 512px wide is roughly 50-80k image tokens depending on aspect ratio.\\r\\n- The transcript is cheap (a few thousand tokens at most for a 10-minute video).\\r\\n- Bumping `--resolution` to 1024 roughly quadruples the image tokens per frame. Only do it when necessary.\\r\\n\\r\\nIf you already watched a video this session and the user asks a follow-up, do **not** re-run the script — you already have the frames and transcript in context.
